Maternally separated female rats showed an increased visceromotor response to colorectal distension compared to nonhandled females, indicating stress-induced colorectal hypersensitivity restricted to females.
Maternally separated females had markedly higher jejunal eosinophil infiltration than maternally separated males.
Eosinophil peroxidase activity, a marker of eosinophil activation, was increased in the jejunum of maternally separated females compared to nonhandled females.
Colonic eosinophil density was increased in maternally separated females compared to nonhandled females, with no effect of MS in males.
Jejunal mast cell density was higher in nonhandled females than nonhandled males, and further increased in maternally separated females versus MS males.
Maternally separated females showed increased jejunal mast cell activation (β-hexosaminidase activity) compared with MS males.
Colonic mast cell density was low in nonhandled females compared to males but rose to male levels after maternal separation, with increased β-hexosaminidase activity in MS versus NH females.

Ovariectomy of maternally separated females decreased the visceromotor response to colorectal distension compared to baseline and to sham surgery, indicating reduced visceral sensitivity when ovarian hormones are depleted.

Re-injection of β-estradiol in ovariectomized MS females restored (increased) the visceromotor response compared with before injection and compared with vehicle-treated ovariectomized females, confirming a causal role for estradiol in visceral hypersensitivity.

β-estradiol injection in maternally separated male rats induced a female-like increase in colonic sensitivity, unlike vehicle-treated males, demonstrating that estradiol can induce visceral hypersensitivity even in males.

Ovariectomy did not affect eosinophil or mast cell density in the jejunum or colon of females, indicating the immune infiltration triggered by early-life stress is not reversed by estrogen depletion after puberty.
β-estradiol treatment in maternally separated males increased jejunal eosinophil density and colonic eosinophil and mast cell density, without significant change in activation markers.
β-estradiol-treated males showed increased jejunal mucosal expression of F2rl1 (PAR2) and ccl11 (eotaxin-1), inflammation-related genes.
Colonic mucosal mcpt2 expression showed a nonsignificant trend toward upregulation in β-estradiol-treated males.
Jejunal mucosal GPER receptor expression was increased in maternally separated females compared to nonhandled females.
Colonic mucosal GPER expression was decreased in maternally separated ovariectomized females compared to sham, and its expression positively correlated with colonic sensitivity (AUC of VMR).
Ovariectomy had no effect on gene expression of selected inflammatory markers in jejunal and colonic mucosa of females.
Daily ALCAR administration for 14 days significantly improved erectile function in rats with bilateral cavernous nerve injury at both low and high doses.
Bilateral cavernous nerve injury led to decreased smooth muscle content and increased collagen content in the corpus cavernosum, indicative of fibrosis.
Expression of the fibrosis marker TGF-beta was significantly up-regulated in the corpus cavernosum of BCNI rats compared to sham.
CTGF expression was significantly up-regulated in the corpus cavernosum of BCNI rats.
Administration of low- and high-dose ALCAR alleviated the increased TGF-beta, CTGF, and Smad2/3 fibrosis marker expression seen in BCNI rats.
ALCAR treatment promoted the NO/cGMP signaling pathway in the corpus cavernosum of BCNI rats.
ALCAR treatment increased neuronal nitric oxide synthase (nNOS) expression in the corpus cavernosum of bilateral cavernous nerve injury rats.
ALCAR treatment down-regulated tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) expression in the corpus cavernosum of bilateral cavernous nerve injury rats.
In vitro, ALCAR promoted the migration and proliferation of rat Schwann cell line S16.
ALCAR increased expression of 22-kD peripheral myelin protein (PMP22) and nerve growth factor (NGF) in Schwann cells in vitro.
Rats treated with ALCAR showed high expression of ATF3 and S100 in the distal nerve tissue at the cavernous nerve extrusion site, indicating enhanced nerve regeneration.

Five new patients with 1q41 deletions including TGFB2 are reported, adding to four previously described patients, and the deletion is associated with a neurodevelopmental phenotype including hypotonia, motor delay, speech delay, and intellectual disability.
The smallest deletion region common to all nine patients spans 785 kb and contains only two genes, RRP15 and TGFB2.
Prior mouse studies show that TGFB2 knockout results in severe perinatal anomalies.
TGFB2 is expressed in the embryonic mouse hindbrain floor, suggesting a role in neurodevelopment.
A three-SNP GCH1 haplotype (rs10483639, rs841, rs3783641) was reported to be associated with 30-50% lower BH4 production compared to individuals without the haplotype.

Antoniades et al. identified a similar GCH1 haplotype with genotype frequencies of 70% normal (OO), 27.4% heterozygous (XO), and 2% homozygous (XX), with the XX homozygous genotype showing 80% lower BH4 than the normal OO genotype.

The paper hypothesizes that a marginal BH4 deficiency causes uncoupling of inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) upon SARS-CoV-2-induced activation, producing excess superoxide and peroxynitrite that create a self-perpetuating cycle of oxidative stress underlying PASC.

BH4 synthesis via GCH1 induction is required for effective proliferation of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, and BH4 also modulates T cell function once activated, implying that BH4 deficiency could impair antiviral T cell responses and allow reactivation of latent viruses like EBV during PASC.

AGMO regulation of platelet-activating factor (PAF) is dependent on sufficient BH4 as a cofactor, so BH4 deficiency from GCH1 mutations may prevent AGMO from downregulating heightened PAF levels needed to restore oxidative homeostasis.

The GCH1-BH4-phospholipid axis is described as a master regulator of ferroptosis resistance, such that BH4 shortage may diminish resistance to ferroptosis, releasing DAMPs and sustaining pro-inflammatory activity and organ damage.

Folate-pathway mutations, chiefly MTHFR C677T and A1298C, along with diets deficient in fresh green vegetables, are proposed to reduce dihydrofolate availability needed for the QDPR-mediated recycling of BH2 back into BH4.

Mutations of QDPR (quinoid dihydropteridine reductase) have been shown to impair the recycling of BH2 back into BH4, a pathway that is a major source of BH4 replenishment, particularly after neurotransmitter synthesis.

The paper proposes that BH4-dependent deficiencies in serotonin, dopamine, norepinephrine, and epinephrine (via PAH, TH, TPH) are tied to numerous CNS/PNS dysfunctions associated with PASC, including brain fog, anosmia/dysgeusia, insomnia, dysautonomia, essential tremor, POTS, EDS, and intestinal dysmotility.
The author suggests prescribing tramadol as part of an antioxidant treatment protocol because it has been reported to increase superoxide dismutase and glutathione peroxidase.

The author suggests providing exogenous BH4 (Pteridin-4 OTC sapropterin 2.5 mg or prescription low-dose Kuvan) to recouple eNOS, iNOS, and nNOS as a proposed treatment for the hypothesized self-perpetuating oxidative stress in PASC.
The author suggests supplementing with quercetin and resveratrol as antioxidants to stimulate immune regulators to downregulate iNOS as part of a proposed PASC treatment approach.
The author suggests restoring the methylation cycle with l-methylfolate and hydroxycobalamin (B12) to increase BH4 through de novo production and recycling in patients with PASC.

Robust regression of high-resolution EGG spatial slow wave features against symptom severity showed a highly accurate fit (r=0.8) in one subgroup of gastroparesis/functional dyspepsia patients, indicating their symptoms are well explained by gastric myoelectric dysfunction.

A subgroup of seven patients had spatial slow wave features within the normal range of controls despite symptom severity that significantly exceeded what these slow wave features predicted, suggesting gastric myoelectric dysfunction is not the prominent etiology in this subgroup.

Among five patients re-assessed with validated symptom questionnaires after pyloric and prokinetic interventions, those whose symptom severity had exceeded the regression line (i.e., not explained by myoelectric dysfunction) reported symptom improvement.

Among the same five re-assessed patients, those whose symptoms lay close to the regression line (i.e., explained by myoelectric dysfunction) experienced no improvement after pyloric and prokinetic interventions.
At baseline, gene expression levels including Mmp2, Tgfb2, and other TGFβ-signaling genes did not differ significantly between untreated LDS (Tgfbr2-mutant) and wild-type mouse tendons.

Six weeks after patellar tendon transection, Mmp2 expression remained persistently elevated compared with baseline in LDS (Tgfbr2-mutant) tendons, an effect not observed in wild-type tendons undergoing the same procedure.
Six weeks after patellar tendon transection, Tgfb2 expression remained persistently elevated compared with baseline in LDS (Tgfbr2-mutant) tendons, an effect not observed in wild-type tendons.
Untreated LDS tendons showed significantly greater cellularity and cell rounding on histology compared with untreated wild-type tendons at baseline.

Both wild-type and LDS tendons showed significantly worse histologic healing scores after patellar tendon transection surgery compared with untreated tendons, with the differential response between genotypes suggesting impaired healing quality in LDS.

The study provides the first mechanistic insight into how Loeys-Dietz syndrome (caused by TGFβ pathway mutations, modeled via Tgfbr2 mutation) affects tendon structure and healing, potentially explaining clinical tendon/ligament dysfunction and joint laxity seen in LDS patients.
The authors conclude that baseline morphologic differences between LDS and WT tendons may help explain the increased risk of tendon/ligament dysfunction seen in patients with Loeys-Dietz syndrome.
The differential post-injury healing response observed in LDS tendons is proposed to account for delayed tendon healing and production of weaker repair tissue in LDS.
Gastric biopsy HSV-1 DNA was detected in 100% of FGID+FM patients versus 26.7% of controls, a highly significant association.
Gastric HSV-1 DNA was detected in 80% of FGID-only (no FM) patients versus 26.7% of controls, a significant association.
ICP8 protein, a marker of active HSV-1 lytic replication, was detected in 83.3% of FGID+FM patients versus 6.7% of controls.
ICP8 protein was detected in 73.3% of FGID-only patients versus 6.7% of controls, indicating active HSV-1 replication.
Across all study groups, gastric ICP8 (active HSV-1 replication) presence was significantly associated with irritable bowel syndrome specifically.
Histologically identified gastritis was common in both FGID+FM patients and controls and was not significantly associated with FGID+FM status.
Histologically identified gastritis was present in 100% of FGID-only patients but was not significantly associated with FGID status versus controls.
H. pylori infection was less prevalent in FGID+FM patients than controls and was not significantly associated with FGID+FM status.
H. pylori infection was not significantly associated with FGID-only status versus controls.
Among the nine human herpesviruses, HSV-1 was the only one detected by DNA sequencing in any gastric biopsy PCR product across all study groups.
Coinfection with H. pylori and HSV-1 in the same gastric biopsy was rare, occurring in 6.7% of FGID+FM patients, 13.3% of FGID-only patients, and no controls.

In rounds 3-5, 37.7% of people with prior COVID-19 reported one or more of 29 symptoms persisting at 12 weeks, and 17.5% reported three or more, corresponding to population prevalences of 5.80% and 2.23% respectively.
In the round 6 replication sample (May 2021), persistent symptom prevalence at 12 weeks was lower than in rounds 3-5, at 21.6% for 1+ symptoms and 11.9% for 3+ symptoms.
Tiredness was the most prevalent persistent symptom at 12 weeks, but its prevalence declined by more than half between rounds 3-5 (16.8%) and round 6 (8.0%).
Female sex was independently associated with higher risk of persistent symptoms at 12 weeks in age-sex and mutually adjusted logistic regression.
Prior hospitalisation with COVID-19 was the strongest single risk factor for persistent symptoms at 12 weeks, more than tripling the odds.
Asian ethnicity was associated with lower risk of persistent symptoms compared to white ethnicity.
Risk of persistent symptoms increased linearly with age in both sexes, by an additional 3.5 percentage points per decade of life.
In GAM modelling, women had approximately 8 percentage points higher risk of persistent symptoms than men across all ages.

Unsupervised clustering identified a large 'tiredness cluster' (Cluster L1, n=15,799) of symptomatic participants at 12 weeks characterised by tiredness co-occurring with muscle aches, difficulty sleeping and shortness of breath.

A second, smaller 'respiratory cluster' (Cluster L2, n=4441) was identified with high prevalence of shortness of breath, tight chest and chest pain, and this cluster had substantially higher rates of prior severe illness and hospitalisation than Cluster L1.

Background prevalence of persistent symptoms (11+ days) in PCR-negative adults in the companion REACT-1 study was ~3%, roughly tenfold lower than the COVID-19-associated persistent symptom prevalence found in REACT-2, indicating most of the excess symptom burden is attributable to COVID-19.

In a sensitivity analysis restricting to participants who self-reported COVID-19 and tested LFIA-antibody-positive, the prevalence of persistent symptoms at 12 weeks was higher than in the main analysis.

Using a reduced set of 15 symptoms associated with self-reported PCR-positivity only slightly reduced estimated persistent symptom prevalence at 12 weeks and identified the same risk factors as the full 29-symptom analysis.

Multivariable variable-selection analysis ranked age, sex, BMI, household income, healthcare/care home worker status, deprivation, smoking status, prior hospitalisation, and vaping status as the strongest predictors of persistent COVID-19 symptoms, in that order.

In the round 6 replication analysis, smoking, vaping and deprivation were no longer significantly associated with persistent symptoms in multiple logistic regression, unlike in the rounds 3-5 main analysis.
Symptom prevalence dropped rapidly by 4 weeks post-onset, declined further by 12 weeks, but then plateaued with limited further decline up to ~22 weeks in both sexes.
ME/CFS patients showed significantly reduced cortical volume in the left caudal middle frontal region compared with healthy controls.
ME/CFS patients showed significantly reduced cortical thickness in the right precuneus region compared with healthy controls.
Left amygdala volume was significantly larger in ME/CFS patients than in healthy controls, and this finding survived multiple comparison correction.

Corpus callosum central region, left and right hemisphere, and whole cortex volumes appeared lower in ME/CFS than HC only before multiple comparison correction, and were not significant after correction.
Fatigue score showed a significantly different (abnormal) regression relationship with cortical volume/thickness in ME/CFS compared with HC in the right postcentral gyrus and inferior parietal lobe.
Heart rate variability (HRV) showed a significantly different relationship with cortical thickness in ME/CFS versus HC in the right superior parietal and left superior frontal gyrus.

Heart rate (HR) showed abnormal (group-different) relationships with cortical volume/thickness in ME/CFS in bilateral lateral occipital and right caudal middle frontal thickness, and left paracentral gyrus volume.

Sleep disturbance score (SDS) showed abnormal group-different relationships with cortical volume in left lateral occipital and superior frontal gyrus, and with cortical thickness in the right lingual gyrus.

Respiratory rate (Resp) showed abnormal group-different relationships with cortical volume in left caudal middle frontal and right superior frontal gyrus, and with thickness in left rostral middle frontal and superior frontal gyrus.
SF-36 mental score (Ment_all) showed an abnormal group-different relationship with cortical volume in the right inferior parietal lobe.

The authors hypothesize that stress-related increased amygdala volume in ME/CFS may be mediated by altered brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) expression, citing prior literature reporting BDNF alteration in ME/CFS.
Serum activin A was significantly elevated in ME/CFS patients compared with healthy controls, with 67% of cases above the normal range.
Gulf War Illness veterans also showed significantly elevated serum activin A compared with controls, at levels comparable to ME/CFS.
Serum IL-21 was significantly elevated in ME/CFS patients relative to healthy controls, with 86% of cases above the normal range.
Despite elevated IL-21, serum CXCL13 was not significantly different between ME/CFS and controls, suggesting impaired TFH/germinal center function.
Serum activin A was significantly higher in ME/CFS cases seropositive for EBV and/or HHV-6A dUTPase antibodies compared with seronegative ME/CFS cases.
Serum IL-21 was significantly higher in ME/CFS cases seropositive for EBV/HHV-6A dUTPase antibodies compared with seronegative cases.
Serum from ME/CFS patients induced differentiation of naive CD4+ T cells into TFH-like cells (PD-1+CXCR5+) in vitro, enhanced further by IL-12.
Blocking activin A with follistatin-315 significantly decreased ME/CFS serum-induced TFH cell differentiation and IL-21 secretion, confirming an activin A-dependent mechanism.
EBV and HHV-6A dUTPase proteins strongly induced activin A secretion from human dendritic cells, far more than human control dUTPase.
EBV and HHV-6A dUTPase proteins induced secretion of BAFF and pentraxin-3 from human dendritic cells, molecules important for TFH and B cell differentiation.
Conditioned media from dendritic cells treated with EBV or HHV-6A dUTPase induced TFH cell marker expression (PD-1, ICOS, CXCR5) in naive CD4+ T cells, enhanced further with IL-12.
EBV dUTPase-conditioned DC media increased IL-21 secretion by activated naive CD4+ T cells relative to control conditioned media.
EBV dUTPase-conditioned DC media enhanced CXCL13 secretion by TFH-differentiated CD4+ T cells, demonstrating functional B cell help capacity.
EBV and HHV-6A dUTPase conditioned media increased IL-10 secretion by activated naive CD4+ T cells, a cytokine that supports B cell survival and class-switching.

Pathway analysis of dUTPase-induced dendritic cell secretome showed significant enrichment for pattern recognition receptor signaling, T helper differentiation, IL-12 signaling, NF-κB signaling, and DC maturation pathways.
In vivo, mice injected with EBV dUTPase protein showed significantly increased splenic CD4+ T cells expressing TFH markers IL-21, BCL6, and CXCR5 compared with vehicle-injected mice.
EBV dUTPase injection significantly increased the frequency of follicular helper NKT (iNKTFH) cells in mouse spleen compared with vehicle, supporting an extrafollicular antibody response mechanism.
EBV dUTPase injection significantly increased the frequency of marginal zone B cells and MZ B/precursor subsets in mouse spleen relative to vehicle, without affecting follicular B cell subsets.
EBV dUTPase injection increased splenic germinal center B cell frequencies, plasmablasts, plasma cells, and total germinal center number, along with increased CD4+ T cell infiltration into GCs.
Spleen lysate IL-21 concentration was significantly higher in mice injected with EBV dUTPase compared with vehicle controls.
Genes encoding IL-7 and IL-11, involved in B and T cell development, were significantly downregulated in splenocytes of mice injected with EBV dUTPase.
EBV dUTPase increased mRNA expression of multiple genes involved in B cell activation, germinal center development, and TFH interaction in splenic pan-B-enriched cells.
EBV dUTPase downregulated Cdkn1a, Fas, Cxcr4, and Flt3 mRNA expression in splenic pan-B-enriched cells, including Cxcr4 which is important for B cell dark-zone trafficking.
EBV dUTPase upregulated TFH-associated genes (Pd-1, Cd40l, Il21, Ox40/Tnfrsf4, Xbp1) in splenic CD4+ T/NKT-enriched cells, consistent with in vitro human TFH differentiation data.
Studies of muscle and leukocyte mitochondria in ME/CFS patients found enriched mitochondrial cristae, mtDNA polymorphisms, and links between specific mtDNA haplotypes and symptoms.

Studies on leukocyte ATP synthesis in ME/CFS patients reported conflicting results (both increases and decreases), while elevated CSF lactate suggested impaired oxidative phosphorylation and increased anaerobic metabolism.
Decreases in NADH and CoQ10 levels have been observed in patients with ME/CFS.
Mandarano et al. reported reduced mitochondrial membrane potential in CD8+ T cells of ME/CFS patients both at rest and during activation.

Hornig showed impaired resting glycolysis in CD4+ and CD8+ T cells of ME/CFS patients, with CD8+ T cells also showing impaired activation-related metabolic remodeling and reduced mitochondrial membrane potential.
Hornig suggested that mitochondrial ROS activate NLRP3 inflammasomes in ME/CFS patients, driving release of IL-1β and IL-18 and inducing inflammation.
A double-blind randomized controlled trial of rituximab in ME/CFS patients failed to confirm efficacy.
Supplements such as NADH, CoQ10, and acetyl L-carnitine showed some efficacy in ME/CFS but their effects were limited.

Mice given hydrogen-rich water during 4 weeks of stress-induced swimming showed higher swimming endurance, lower blood glucose/lactate/BUN, higher liver glycogen and serum LDH, lower NO, higher GPx, and lower inflammatory cytokines than placebo water.
In rats subjected to acute treadmill exercise, H2 gas inhalation suppressed exercise-induced increases in TNF-α, IL-6, TBARS, and CREB phosphorylation while further increasing SOD.

Intravenous hydrogen-containing saline significantly inhibited 8-OHdG elevation in racehorses at all measured time points after a high-intensity race, though BAP and d-ROM did not differ from placebo.

In racehorses, oral HRW slightly reduced d-ROM and significantly increased BAP/d-ROM around treadmill exercise, though the authors themselves questioned the clinical significance given the small effect size.

In athletes, HRW ingestion before cycle ergometer and knee extension exercise significantly suppressed increases in blood lactate and inhibited the initial decrease in peak torque, without changing d-ROM, BAP, or creatine kinase.
HRW ingestion significantly lowered psychological fatigue in untrained subjects and improved endurance/fatigue metrics in trained participants during exercise.
HRW administration before progressively increasing exercise intensity significantly lowered blood lactate, ventilatory equivalent of oxygen, and rating of perceived exertion versus placebo.
Inhaled H2 gas during a 60-minute recovery period after intense exercise significantly reduced urinary 8-OHdG excretion and increased countermovement jump height versus placebo gas.
During 3 days of continuous exercise, HRW significantly suppressed the decrease in BAP/d-ROM antioxidant capacity seen in the placebo group.
Two weeks of continuous HRW intake significantly increased peak oxygen uptake and slightly increased peak load during gradual cycling exercise compared to placebo water.
Weekly nanobubbled HRW intake enhanced anaerobic test performance (increased peak/average power, reduced fatigue index) in trained cyclists but not in untrained subjects.
Two weeks of HRW ingestion attenuated the decline in peak power output seen in placebo during repeated sprints to exhaustion in trained cyclists.

In an open-label multicenter trial, COVID-19 patients treated with H2/O2 mixed gas showed significantly greater improvements in disease severity, dyspnea, cough, chest distress/pain, and oxygen saturation than controls.

A randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 14 days of H2 gas inhalation (2x60 min/day) in 50 acute post-COVID-19 patients significantly improved physical and respiratory function on gait and pulmonary function tests versus placebo gas.
Despite symptom similarities between long COVID/post-COVID and ME/CFS, the authors state there is currently no evidence that COVID-19 is a trigger for ME/CFS.

Pharmacokinetic comparison in rats showed higher peak blood/tissue H2 concentrations with oral HRW than gas inhalation, but a markedly greater area-under-curve with H2 gas inhalation over time, suggesting gas inhalation delivers more sustained systemic H2 exposure.
Nearly all participants with ME/CFS reported problems performing usual activities, with over half completely unable to do so.
Pain and discomfort was the second most affected EQ-5D dimension, with the large majority of ME/CFS patients experiencing some or extreme pain.
Mobility was impaired in the large majority of ME/CFS patients, some confined to bed.
Self-care difficulties (washing/dressing) affected two thirds of participants with ME/CFS.
Anxiety and depression was the least affected EQ-5D dimension but still impacted the majority of ME/CFS patients.
The average health-status VAS score of ME/CFS patients was markedly lower than the UK general population norm.
Mean EQ-5D health-state value for ME/CFS patients was markedly lower than the UK representative population value.
Nearly half of ME/CFS participants reported having another chronic health condition in addition to ME/CFS.
The study confirmed a strong female preponderance among people with ME/CFS in this large international sample.
Family members of people with ME/CFS reported a high overall FROM-16 quality-of-life impact score, indicating major impairment.
Worry was the emotion most frequently impacted among family members of ME/CFS patients.
Frustration and sadness were also highly prevalent emotional impacts reported by family members.
Family activities and holidays were the most impacted areas in family members' personal and social life due to a relative's ME/CFS.
A substantial majority of family members reported that finances and sex life were negatively affected by their relative's ME/CFS.
Worse patient overall health status (lower VAS) was significantly correlated with greater negative impact on family member quality of life.
A moderate significant negative correlation was found between patients' EQ-5D health utility values and family members' FROM-16 impact scores.
There was no significant difference between the family impact reported in this large international study and a smaller prior pilot study of UK ME/CFS families.
Family members of ME/CFS patients had a significantly higher (worse) FROM-16 impact score than family members of cancer patients.
Family members of ME/CFS patients reported significantly greater QoL impact than family members/partners of COVID-19 survivors in a comparable international study.
A genome-wide association study found nominally significant association of ME/CFS with 65 SNPs, including markers in the clock gene NPAS2, though this did not survive genome-wide correction.
In a gene-expression study of peripheral blood cells from the same cohort, ME/CFS patients showed 10-fold higher expression of NPAS2 compared to controls.
In the UK Biobank study of activity levels in ~85,000 people, the same NPAS2 SNP identified in the ME/CFS GWAS was nominally associated with activity level.
Twin studies indicate ME/CFS has a heritable component accounting for 55% of the phenotypic variance.
Actigraphy over 5-7 days in 8 ME/CFS patients and 10 controls (predominantly female adults) showed lower daytime activity and less regularity across days in activity cycles in the ME/CFS group.

In a study of 15 ME/CFS patients and 15 controls over 5 days, ME/CFS patients reported earlier sleep times and less quality sleep, but there were no differences in overall activity or activity rhythms.

In 10 middle-aged women with ME/CFS versus 10 matched controls, the ME/CFS group showed longer sleep latency, more waking after sleep onset, more time in bed, later wake times, decreased total activity, lower activity rhythm amplitude, and less stable rhythms.

The same study found less light exposure among ME/CFS patients and irregular coupling of activity and temperature rhythms, with ME/CFS patients lacking the midday temperature increase seen in controls and showing a distinct evening temperature drop.

In 20 ME/CFS patients and 17 matched controls, no differences were identified in core temperature rhythms or DLMO timing, but the significant positive correlation between temperature acrophase and DLMO seen in controls was absent in ME/CFS.

In 10 ambulatory ME/CFS patients versus 10 controls monitored by telemetry over 48 hours, temperature rhythms were similar, with only a trend toward more variability and more frequent ultradian rhythms among ME/CFS patients.
In 30 ME/CFS patients versus 72 controls, evening cortisol levels were reduced in ME/CFS, also confirmed by 24-hour urine cortisol measurement.
In the same HPA axis study of 30 ME/CFS patients and 72 controls, ACTH levels were elevated in ME/CFS compared to controls.

In a study of 30 ME/CFS patients and 15 controls sampled 12 hours apart, mean cortisol levels did not differ by group at either time, but the diurnal change in cortisol was higher in controls than in ME/CFS.

In 15 ME/CFS patients without co-morbid psychiatric disorders versus 10 controls, ME/CFS patients had reduced morning ACTH and an earlier acrophase, with no differences in mean cortisol, prolactin, or growth hormone.
In 17 CFS patients versus 12 controls, circadian rhythms in heart rate, systolic and diastolic blood pressure showed significantly higher amplitudes in patients, leading to nighttime hypotension.
A 12-week trial of melatonin therapy in ME/CFS patients did not achieve overall symptom reduction.
A 12-week light therapy trial (2500 lux, lower than the typical clinical 10,000 lux) did not reduce overall ME/CFS symptoms but did improve sleep.
A subset of ME/CFS patients with phase-delayed circadian rhythms showed a preferential response to melatonin therapy over 3 months.

Graded exercise therapy has shown beneficial effects on fatigue, sleep, and mood in some ME/CFS studies, but may worsen post-exertional fatigue symptoms in others, making its role in treating ME/CFS controversial.

A meta-analysis of 38 studies examining 77 different cytokines found that the majority of studies of pro-inflammatory markers IL-1β, IL-6 and TNF failed to identify significant differences between ME/CFS and controls.

In a large study of 298 adult ME/CFS cases and 348 controls, differences were found in IL-1β, IL-6, TNF and other cytokines associated with duration of illness, with more pronounced changes in early-stage (<3 years) versus chronic cases.
IL-1β, IL-6 and TNF were associated with severity of sleep disturbance and fatigue among ME/CFS cases.
Meta-analysis found the strongest and most consistent cytokine support for ME/CFS involvement was TGFB, with elevated TGFB reported in five of eight studies and no studies showing decreased levels.
In a subsequent independent study of 584 adults, TGFB was significantly increased in ME/CFS cases compared to controls, replicating prior meta-analytic findings.
Across most studies of ME/CFS, TGFB was not associated with fatigue severity or exercise, but was associated with symptoms of pain and cognitive processing deficits.
Across most ME/CFS studies, serum TGFB levels were not associated with fatigue severity or with exercise capacity.
TGFB levels were significantly associated with pain and cognitive processing deficits in ME/CFS patients.

In mice, intracerebroventricular injection of TGFB reproduced several ME/CFS-like features including reduced forced-swim activity, increased pain sensitivity, elevated peripheral muscle fatigue markers, and decreased striatal dopamine.
In adolescents with ME/CFS, TGFB was not significantly different from controls but correlated with stress biomarkers and fatigue scores.
Resistin was the only other serum marker besides TGFB that distinguished ME/CFS cases from controls in the largest human cytokine study.

Seventeen additional peptides (chemokines CCL11, CXCL1, CXCL10; interleukins IL-4, IL-5, IL-7, IL-12p70, IL-13, IL-17F, interferon-alpha; leptin; and growth factors G-CSF, GM-CSF, LIF, NGF, TGFA, SCF), though not significantly different from controls, were significantly associated with ME/CFS illness severity.

TGFB protein is rhythmically expressed with age-dependent circadian oscillation in the SCN and paraventricular nucleus of young mice, but these rhythms are lost in older animals which show higher, constant expression, suggesting a developmentally limited CNS role.
Serum TGFB1 levels show diurnal (circadian) variation in human subjects.

In response to alkaline pH, fibroblasts signal via TGFB1/SMAD2/3 to upregulate DEC1 and phase-shift circadian rhythms, an effect reproduced by pulsatile 1-hour treatment with recombinant TGFB1 peptide.
Prolonged exposure (>4 hours) to TGFB2 strongly inhibited clock gene expression (PER1, PER3, CRY1) in peripheral fibroblasts and neurons, in contrast to short TGFB1 exposures.

TGFB2 was identified as the active paracrine component synchronizing circadian rhythms across peripheral cell networks, upregulating PER2 expression via TGFBR1, SMAD3/4, and CRE DNA-binding sites in U2OS Bmal:luc reporter cells.
In humans undergoing experimental circadian disruption, resistin levels increased and were associated with elevated blood pressure and decreased vagal modulation of heart rate.
Shift workers showed 18% higher resistin levels than daytime workers in a community study of 439 shift workers versus 255 daytime workers.
The cytokine CXCL1 is increased in arrhythmic clock-mutant mice.
Both G-CSF and CCL11 (Eotaxin-1) are increased by peripheral-central circadian rhythm desynchronization in animal models.
SARS-CoV nucleocapsid protein alters TGFB signaling pathways by directly interacting with SMAD3-4 proteins, a mechanism proposed to promote viral proliferation by reducing apoptosis.
SARS-CoV-2 upregulates TGFB expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells, alveolar cells, and plasma cells of infected hosts.

Among survivors of the 2003 SARS pandemic in Hong Kong, 27-40% of confirmed cases met criteria for ME/CFS more than 3 years after recovery, with high rates of comorbid PTSD (54%), depression (39%), somatoform pain (36%), and panic disorder (34%).

In a Canadian cohort of SARS survivors, 8% of total cases (22/273) remained disabled by core ME/CFS symptoms (fatigue, myalgia, weakness, depression, sleep abnormalities) 13-36 months after infection.
Recent studies indicate that 40-60% of people with COVID-19 continue to have significant symptoms months after initial illness, a syndrome termed post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) or long COVID.
In an online survey of 640 people self-reporting PASC symptoms, Vitamin D deficiency was reported in 13.4% of respondents, similar to general population estimates.
A meta-analysis of SARS-CoV-2 infections confirmed that Vitamin D deficiency was associated with severe COVID-19 disease.
A prospective study of 149 PASC patients followed for a median of 79 days found no correlation between Vitamin D deficiency and fatigue.
In a study of 25,534 individuals, low 25-OH Vitamin D combined with low light exposure (but not Vitamin D status alone) was linked with excessive sleep duration.
Shift workers are at increased risk for developing COVID-19, even after correcting for sleep duration.
Hospitalization, especially need for critical care, has been associated with higher rates of developing PASC.
Ability to maintain physiological circadian rhythms has been associated with better outcomes in the ICU.

A single 60-mg oral dose of pyridostigmine increased peak exercise oxygen uptake (Vo2) compared with a decrease seen after placebo in ME/CFS subjects undergoing repeated invasive cardiopulmonary exercise testing.
Peak-versus-rest Vo2 was significantly greater in the pyridostigmine group than in the placebo group on the second exercise test.
Exercise cardiac output declined less after pyridostigmine than after placebo, indicating relative preservation of cardiac output with cholinergic stimulation.
Right atrial pressure increased after pyridostigmine but decreased after placebo, suggesting improved right ventricular filling with cholinergic stimulation.

The authors interpret the improvement in peak Vo2, cardiac output, and right ventricular filling pressures with pyridostigmine as evidence that treatable neurovascular dysregulation underlies acute exercise intolerance in ME/CFS.

Worsening of peak exercise Vo2, cardiac output, and right atrial pressure following placebo (i.e., across repeated exercise testing without treatment) may signal the physiological onset of postexertional malaise.
Serum levels of the autophagy protein ATG13 are strongly elevated in ME/CFS patients compared to age-matched healthy controls.
Serum from ME/CFS patients induces production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and nitric oxide (NO) in human HMC3 microglial cells, an effect attributable to ATG13.
Neutralizing ATG13 in ME/CFS patient serum strongly reduces the ROS and NO production induced in HMC3 microglial cells, supporting a causal role for ATG13 in this stress response.
ATG13 binds and employs the Receptor for Advanced Glycation End-products (RAGE) to stimulate ROS production in microglial cells, implicating RAGE signaling as the mechanistic link.
Population-based prevalence estimates of Long COVID among adults are cited as centering around 20%, with wide variability across studies.
People affected by Long COVID commonly report fatigue, shortness of breath, cognitive dysfunction, sleep disorders, pain, or inability to return to work or normal social life.
A prior survey (NIHR) found that Long COVID affected patients' ability to work in 80% of respondents.
The same prior survey found that Long COVID affected patients' family life in 71% of respondents.

A longitudinal cohort study cited in the discussion found that 2-4% of children enrolled during the first and second pandemic waves reported at least one symptom persisting beyond 12 weeks post-infection.

Among 241 online survey respondents rating 68 research questions for importance (1-5), the question on effective treatment/rehabilitation approaches for Long COVID (A5.1) received the highest importance rating.
The research question asking whether diagnostic criteria for Long COVID differ between men and women (A3.3) received the lowest importance rating among all 68 questions.

Patients with Long COVID and patients with ME/CFS were reported to share several common symptoms as well as strategies to overcome stigmatisation, motivating inclusion of ME/CFS patients in the citizen science process.
The patient's serum free testosterone was markedly decreased to 5.5 pg/mL, meeting the Japanese diagnostic criteria for late-onset hypogonadism.
MRI revealed a partially empty sella with anterior pituitary atrophy, suggesting pituitary structural involvement underlying the patient's hypogonadism.
Serum FSH was persistently low and LH secretion showed a delayed response to GnRH stimulation, consistent with hypothalamic hypogonadism.
Anterior pituitary responses to CRH and TRH stimulation tests were almost normal, indicating preserved corticotroph and thyrotroph function.
Bone mineral density was reduced to 73% of the young adult mean in the lumbar spine and 87% in the femur, indicating a possible skeletal complication of hypogonadism.
Treatment with hochuekkito, a Japanese Kampo herbal medicine, was followed by gradual improvement in the patient's symptoms and AMS score alongside a rise in serum free testosterone.
Juzentaihoto, another Kampo medicine, was added about two months into treatment based on traditional signs of 'qi deficiency' and 'blood deficiency'.
Repeated GnRH tests over three phases of treatment showed that LH responsiveness to GnRH gradually improved, whereas the FSH peak response remained unchanged.
Reported literature indicates that up to 13-45% of patients with long COVID meet diagnostic criteria for ME/CFS.
SARS-CoV-2 enters host cells via ACE2 receptors, which are abundantly expressed by testicular Leydig cells, suggesting a mechanism for direct viral involvement causing primary hypogonadism.
SARS-CoV-2 has been detected in testicular tissue from cadavers of people who died with COVID-19, supporting direct viral involvement in gonadal dysfunction.

The patient exhibited post-exertional malaise, sleep disturbance, and reduced stamina consistent with ME/CFS criteria, but was ultimately diagnosed with late-onset hypogonadism as an alternative explanation for his persistent fatigue.
The patient's Aging Male's Symptoms (AMS) scale score was 44 out of 85, indicating moderate late-onset hypogonadism syndrome.

After 4 weeks of treatment, patients receiving ginger-indirect moxibustion plus acupuncture showed significantly greater improvement in Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS) scores than those receiving acupuncture alone.

After 2 weeks of treatment, patients receiving ginger-indirect moxibustion plus acupuncture showed significantly greater improvement in SPHERE psychological health scores than those receiving acupuncture alone.
Improvement in depressive symptoms (SDS) did not significantly differ between the ginger-indirect moxibustion plus acupuncture group and the acupuncture-alone group.
Improvement in anxiety symptoms (HAMA) did not significantly differ between the ginger-indirect moxibustion plus acupuncture group and the acupuncture-alone group.
No severe adverse events were reported with ginger-indirect moxibustion plus acupuncture treatment, supporting its safety for CFS.
A heterozygous missense variant in COL3A1 was identified by molecular testing, confirming a diagnosis of vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.

The patient presented with recurrent pulmonary hemorrhage manifesting as intermittent hemoptysis, chest pain, and waxing and waning bilateral pulmonary nodules and cavities with halo sign on CT, attributed to vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
Unlike classical presentations, this patient had no skin hyperextensibility or joint hypermobility, despite confirmed vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
Inflammatory markers including erythrocyte sedimentation rate, C-reactive protein, and interleukin-6 were within normal range despite active pulmonary disease.

Empirical antibacterial, antifungal, antimycobacterial, and anti-parasite treatments failed to resolve the waxing and waning pulmonary lesions, which were later attributed to vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome rather than infection.
A monoallelic CYP21A2 deletion that extends into the adjacent TNXB gene creates a chimeric TNXA/TNXB gene, resulting in tenascin-X haploinsufficiency.

Patients with 21-hydroxylase deficiency (congenital adrenal hyperplasia) who also carry a CYP21A2 deletion extending into TNXB display a phenotype compatible with the hypermobility type of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, termed CAH-X.
The prevalence of CAH-X syndrome was estimated to be around 14-15% in large cohorts of patients with 21-hydroxylase deficiency, though population studies remain scarce.

The proband carried a de novo heterozygous missense variant in COL1A1 (c.3235G>A, p.Gly1079Ser), not present in either parent, classified as pathogenic and associated with a phenotype compatible with OI/EDS overlap syndrome.

Clinical examination revealed joint hypermobility (Beighton score 7/9), pale mildly hyperelastic skin, bilateral ectropion, blue sclerae, scoliotic spine curvature, tooth decay, and mild enamel changes.
DEXA scan showed markedly reduced bone mineral density with femoral BMD Z-score of −4.3 SDS and lumbar Z-score of −3.3 SDS, despite no history of fractures.
The authors' whole exome and deep sequencing study of neuroblastoma found somatic pathogenic mutations in collagen type family genes, including COL1A1, in a subset of high-risk neuroblastomas.
COL1A1 has been reported as a gene regulated by a super enhancer involved in modulating neuroblastoma cell identity, and is described as a predisposition gene in pediatric cancers.

The authors hypothesize that the co-occurrence of the COL1A1 mutation and the patient's prior stage 4 MYCN-nonamplified neuroblastoma may not be incidental, though this remains speculative based on a single case.

Growth hormone treatment attempts in OI patients have shown a lack of effectiveness, despite usually normal GH secretion rates, with growth velocity response likely dependent on the underlying disease severity.

Literature review identified 23 individuals with the p.Gly1079Ser COL1A1 mutation, all classified as OI subtypes: 8 with type IV OI, 14 with type I OI, and 1 undetermined, showing broad phenotypic variability including within the same family.

Short stature is rarely seen in EDS overall, except in the spondylodysplastic EDS type 3 caused by recessive loss-of-function variants in the zinc transporter gene SLC39A13, whereas short stature is a common feature among OI/EDS overlap syndrome patients.

Morlino et al. proposed major diagnostic criteria for COL1-related overlap disorder (C1ROD)—blue sclerae, flatfeet with valgus deformity, generalized joint hypermobility for age, and significantly soft/doughy or hyperextensible skin—and minor criteria including short stature, hearing loss, dolichostenomelia, atrophic scars, fractures, and joint dislocations, to guide molecular testing decisions.
There were no significant differences in wound complications or reoperation rates between EDS patients undergoing simple surgery versus complex surgery of the craniocervical junction.
Myofascial flap closure in complex surgery reduced complication rates to a level comparable to simple surgery with traditional closure, showing no significant difference between the two groups.
The CSF cutaneous fistula rate in this EDS cohort undergoing myofascial flap closure was 0%, considerably lower than rates reported in the general literature.
A single patient who developed a postoperative pseudomeningocele secondary to a dural leak had its progression prevented by the myofascial flap closure.
A likely pathogenic nonsense mutation in CHST14 (c.958C>T, p.Arg320*) was identified in the fetus, inherited from the mother.

A novel missense variant in CHST14 (c.896A>G, p.Tyr299Cys) of uncertain significance by ACMG criteria was identified in the fetus, inherited from the father, and predicted to be disease-causing/probably damaging by in silico tools.

The fetus was found to carry compound heterozygous CHST14 mutations (one from each parent), consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance of musculocontractural EDS presenting with bilateral clubfeet and renal pelvis separation.
Pathogenic CHST14 mutations are proposed to cause deficiency of the D4ST1 enzyme, leading to decreased proteoglycans and abnormal collagen fibril assembly that gives rise to mcEDS.

In a prior cohort of 66 mcEDS patients (Minatogawa et al., 2021), 95% (59/62) developed clubfoot, whereas renal structural abnormalities were not observed in that cohort, making the renal pelvis separation in this fetus a notable atypical feature.
Connective tissue disorders involving collagen and elastin assembly defects, including Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, predispose patients to thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm and dissection.

In patients with connective tissue disorders, endovascular repair of thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm shows higher rates of reinterventions and postoperative complications with disputable long-term durability compared to open surgical repair.

Open surgical repair with extensive aortic replacement is considered the standard approach for connective tissue disorder patients with thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm to reduce long-term complications from progressive dilatation of remnant aortic segments.
Small RNA-sequencing of whole blood identified 26 downregulated and 43 upregulated miRNAs in women with fibromyalgia compared to female healthy controls.
Nineteen CholinomiRs (miRNAs predicted to target five or more cholinergic genes) were differentially expressed in FMS blood, comprising 12 upregulated and 7 downregulated miRs.
CholinomiRs were significantly enriched among differentially expressed miRNAs in FMS compared to non-DE miRs, indicating the signature is not due to chance.

Linear discriminant analysis using the 19 CholinomiRs (versus all DE miRs) better separated FMS patients stratified by daily-life pain impairment from controls, with severely impaired FMS patients showing no overlap with controls.

Of the 19 FMS CholinomiRs, 13 were also detected in blood of female Parkinson's disease patients, but none were significantly dysregulated except hsa-miR-128-3p, which showed a trend toward downregulation opposite to its upregulation in FMS.
Hsa-miR-625-5p showed a trend towards downregulation in PD patients reporting pain-related impairment, consistent with its downregulation observed in FMS.
Hsa-miR-27b-3p expression moderately correlated with pain intensity (NRSPain) in FMS patients.
Hsa-miR-148a-3p expression moderately correlated with pain intensity (NRSPain) in FMS patients.
qRT-PCR validated the RNA-seq finding of hsa-miR-182-5p upregulation in FMS, showing an approximately twofold increase compared to controls.
BMPR2 mRNA, predicted target of ten CholinomiRs (eight upregulated), was significantly downregulated in FMS whole blood compared to controls.
IL6ST mRNA, a target of five upregulated CholinomiRs, was significantly downregulated in FMS whole blood compared to controls.
RORA mRNA expression, despite being a target of seven CholinomiRs, did not differ significantly between FMS and healthy controls in whole blood.
NR1D2 mRNA expression did not differ significantly between FMS patients and controls, despite being a predicted target of hsa-miR-182-5p and other CholinomiRs.
None of the other investigated cholinergic-related transcripts (AChE, BDNF, NGFR, BMP3, SRSF6) showed altered mRNA levels in FMS whole blood compared to controls.
Serum total, AChE-specific, and BChE-specific cholinesterase enzymatic activities were similar between FMS patients and healthy controls.

Cross-referencing the 47 predicted cholinergic mRNA targets with Human Protein Atlas blood cell data showed NK cells expressed the highest proportion of these targets, followed by neutrophils, with myeloid dendritic cells expressing the fewest.
Hsa-miR-183-5p, a CholinomiR restricted predominantly to red blood cells, exhibited one of the highest expression levels of all CholinomiRs across sequenced samples.
Low-frequency CholinomiRs showed restricted cell-type distribution, with hsa-miR-548d-5p limited to monocytes and hsa-miR-3609 abundant only in CD4+ T cells.

The nicotinic acetylcholine receptor subunit gene CHRNB2 was a predicted target exclusively of downregulated CholinomiRs, suggesting potential upregulation of this receptor in FMS, though transcript levels were too low to confirm by qRT-PCR.

The study notes that amitriptyline, an anticholinergic first-line pharmacological treatment for FMS, may have a pathophysiological link to CholinomiR-regulated pathways, though only a small number of patients were on the drug and its influence could not be formally assessed.
Low-dose naltrexone is described as a promising novel therapy for fibromyalgia symptoms.
Cannabinoid-based therapies are highlighted as a promising novel treatment approach for fibromyalgia.
Functional imaging studies have identified multiple brain network abnormalities in fibromyalgia that may serve as targets for mechanism-based therapies.
Currently approved pharmacological therapies for fibromyalgia have limited but proven effectiveness overall.
Central sensitization to nociceptive and non-nociceptive stimuli is described as a critical mechanism underlying fibromyalgia, resulting in widespread sensory hypersensitivity.

In the MAPP Symptom Patterns Study cohort, UCPPS patients were classified by self-report questionnaires into four pain mechanism categories: 43% nociceptive-only, 8% neuropathic-only, 27% nociceptive+nociplastic, and 22% neuropathic+nociplastic.

Among the pain mechanism subgroups, nociceptive-only UCPPS patients had the least severe symptoms overall, while neuropathic+nociplastic patients had the most severe symptoms across multiple outcome measures.
Neuropathic pain classification (via painDETECT) in UCPPS patients was associated with genital pain and/or increased sensitivity on pelvic examination.

Nociplastic pain classification (via fibromyalgia survey criteria) in UCPPS patients was associated with comorbid pain conditions, psychosocial difficulties, and increased pressure pain sensitivity outside the pelvic region.
In a cross-sectional survey on complimentary medicine use in rheumatology, 31.8% of patients reported using alternative therapies for pain management.
A self-reported study found 13% of fibromyalgia patients used cannabinoids, with 80% using herbal cannabis, 24% using prescription cannabinoids, and 3% using both.

CB1 receptors expressed on chondrocytes and osteocytes facilitate fibroblast-like synoviocyte adhesion to fibronectin and reduce their migratory capacity, potentially decreasing cartilage destruction.
CB1 activation reduces TRPV1 activity, leading to reduced IL-6 secretion from sensitised fibroblast-like synoviocytes.
Polymorphisms in CNR2 at positions 63 (Q63R) and 316 alter CB2 receptor function, with reduced agonist efficacy for WIN55212-2 and 2-AG at the polymorphic receptor.

In a Lebanese case-control study, the CB2-R63 variant frequency was significantly higher in RA patients than healthy controls, with RR carriers having >10-fold and QR carriers >3-fold risk of RA compared to QQ carriers.

CB2R mRNA and protein expression in synovial tissue and cultured fibroblast-like synoviocytes was slightly higher in RA patients compared to OA patients, and was upregulated by IL-1β, TNF-α or lipopolysaccharide stimulation.

In collagen-induced arthritis mice, the CB2 selective agonist JWH133 suppressed arthritis by decreasing synovial hyperplasia, inflammatory responses, cartilage damage and bone destruction, reducing M1 macrophage infiltration, increasing IL-10, reducing TNF-α/IL-1β/IL-6, and inhibiting osteoclastogenesis via RANKL-induced NF-κB inhibition.
JWH-015 inhibited IL-1β-induced IL-6, IL-8 and COX-2 in human RA synovial fibroblasts and reduced adjuvant-induced arthritis in rats via a glucocorticoid receptor-dependent mechanism.
In a 5-week RCT of 58 RA patients on stable DMARDs, Sativex significantly improved pain (VAS), disease activity (DAS28) and sleep compared to placebo.
The potent FAAH inhibitor PF-04457845 increased AEA levels but showed no significant analgesic effect compared to placebo in osteoarthritis pain.

In a rat monoarthritis model, transdermal CBD significantly reduced joint swelling and pain with decreased immune cell infiltration and synovial membrane thickening, in a dose-dependent manner with no evident side effects.

In a 6-week study of 40 fibromyalgia patients, nabilone was associated with statistically significant improvements in pain (2-point reduction) and a 12-point reduction in Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire score.

A 2011 Barcelona trial in 28 fibromyalgia patients per group found cannabinoids effective for several symptoms including pain and muscle rigidity, though limited by small sample size and short duration.
The National Academies of Sciences, Engineering and Medicine concluded there is moderate-grade evidence supporting the effectiveness of cannabinoids for treatment of fibromyalgia.

Plasma 2-arachidonoylglycerol levels were significantly increased in SLE patients compared to controls and were associated with lower disease activity, while 2-AG metabolism enzymes/receptors were found to be deranged; no differences were seen in AEA, PEA or OEA.

In 190 children with ITP versus 600 healthy controls, the CR2 Q63R missense variant was significantly overrepresented, with the RR genotype and R allele overrepresented in chronic ITP and more than double the risk of chronic form in homozygous carriers.

A systematic review of 118 studies on cannabinoids for musculoskeletal pain found 56% were observational Level-II or below evidence; 72% reported cannabis as effective, 14% mixed effectiveness, 9% not effective, and 4% inconclusive, with 39% reporting mild-to-moderate and 15% possible serious adverse effects.

A systematic review of four trials (including nabilone in 71 fibromyalgia patients and THC/CBD in 58 RA patients) concluded cannabinoids were superior to placebo in neuropathic pain but not in pain due to rheumatic diseases, and evidence remained insufficient for clinical recommendations.

In a 16-week phase 2 RCT of dermatomyositis patients (11 lenabasum, 22 controls), lenabasum showed greater improvement in CDASI damage index and patient-reported skin and overall disease assessments than placebo, with no serious treatment-related adverse events.

A systematic review found the most consistent effects of medical cannabinoids are adverse effects, with a number needed to harm of 8-22 for treatment discontinuation, and 'feeling high' reported in 35-70% of users.
Ever smoking was independently associated with increased odds of having any mosaic chromosomal alteration (mCA) in UK Biobank participants.
Smoking was associated with autosomal mCA, though the effect size was smaller than for overall mCA.
Smoking showed a weak association with mosaic loss-of-X chromosome (mCA-LOX).
Smoking was strongly associated with mosaic loss-of-Y chromosome (mCA-LOY), representing the largest effect among mCA subtypes and likely driving the overall mCA association.
Smoking was associated with increased odds of myeloid-lineage mCA.
Smoking was associated with increased odds of lymphoid-lineage mCA.
There was substantial heterogeneity in the strength of association between smoking and different mCA subclasses, indicating the overall mCA-smoking association was largely driven by mCA-LOY.
Smoking was associated with overall CHIP status in whole-exome sequenced UK Biobank participants.
The strength of association between smoking and CHIP varied significantly by driver gene, showing heterogeneity across CHIP-associated genes.
Mendelian randomization using a genetic instrument for lifetime smoking showed a strong causal association between smoking and mCA overall.
Mendelian randomization supported a causal effect of smoking specifically on mosaic loss-of-Y chromosome (mCA-LOY).
Mendelian randomization did not find a significant causal association between genetically-instrumented smoking and CHIP, in both transethnic and European-ancestry analyses.

The MR-Egger bias intercept test found no evidence of directional pleiotropy across all smoking-somatic mutation comparisons, and alternative MR methods yielded similar results to the primary IVW analysis.

Observational associations between smoking and somatic mutation outcomes remained similar after adjusting for self-reported alcohol consumption, arguing against confounding by this correlated lifestyle factor.
Soluble SCF injected intradermally induced significant vascular leakage (Evans blue extravasation) indicating mast cell activation, while tmSCF-based therapies did not.
tmSCF, tmSCFPLs, and tmSCFNDs did not induce vascular leakage, body temperature drop, or skin edema, unlike soluble SCF, indicating lack of mast cell activation.
Occasional skin irritation and histological edema occurred with soluble SCF treatment but not with tmSCF-based treatments after systemic toxicology dosing.
tmSCF-based treatments showed significantly slower surface c-Kit internalization kinetics than soluble SCF in MC9 mast cells.
tmSCFND treatment showed significantly slower surface c-Kit internalization than soluble SCF in bone marrow mononuclear cells.
In HUVECs, surface c-Kit internalization was significantly slower for tmSCFPL, tmSCFND, and tmSCF compared to soluble SCF.
Mast cells preferentially use the clathrin-mediated pathway to internalize soluble SCF and the caveolin-mediated pathway to internalize tmSCFNDs, while using both pathways for tmSCF or tmSCFPLs.
Bone marrow-derived endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs) preferentially use the clathrin-mediated pathway to uptake soluble SCF but use the caveolin-mediated pathway to uptake tmSCFPLs and tmSCFNDs.
Soluble SCF induced significantly more c-Kit phosphorylation in MC9 mast cells than tmSCF-based treatments, consistent with weaker mast cell activation by tmSCF.
In EPCs, SCF and tmSCFND treatment induced significantly more c-Kit phosphorylation than control, suggesting angiogenic activity via the SCF/c-Kit pathway.
tmSCFPLs induced 16-18 fold greater endothelial tube formation activity than tmSCF protein alone, while tmSCFNDs showed no significant tube formation induction.
None of the SCF/tmSCF-based treatments significantly altered endothelial cell migration or proliferation compared to control.
In a hind limb ischemia model in wild-type mice, tmSCFPL and tmSCFND treatment significantly increased relative blood flow recovery compared to alginate control.
Immunostaining showed significantly increased mature (large, α-SMA+) blood vessels in calf and thigh muscles of WT mice treated with tmSCFPL or tmSCFND compared to control.
SCF expression in endothelial cells was markedly reduced in skin of type 2 diabetic patients compared to non-diabetic patients.
c-Kit expression in endothelial cells was higher in skin from type 2 diabetic patients than non-diabetic patients.
SCF levels in skin fibroblasts were similar between type 2 diabetic and non-diabetic patients.
c-Kit expression in mast cells was increased in skin from diabetic patients compared to non-diabetic patients.
In diabetic ob/ob mice with hind limb ischemia, tmSCFPL and tmSCFND treatment significantly increased blood flow recovery compared to alginate control.

Free tmSCF (without nanocarrier) did not enhance mature blood vessel formation in diabetic ob/ob mice, unlike WT mice, indicating nanocarrier formulation is important for efficacy in diabetic ischemia.
Short-term (30 min) treatment of bone marrow cells with tmSCFPL or tmSCFND increased the CD34−CD133+CD146+ EPC population compared to control or free tmSCF.
Increased CD34+/CD144+ EPCs were found in ischemic muscles of tmSCFND-treated WT mice, indicating EPC recruitment to the ischemic site.
Increased CD34+/CD144+ EPCs were found in ischemic muscles of tmSCF-treated ob/ob mice.
Both tmSCFPLs and tmSCFNDs induced a greater number of large EPC colonies in a colony formation assay compared to control.

A 22-year-old man rapidly developed hives on the trunk and face immediately after subcutaneous ketamine administration for psychiatric treatment, consistent with mast cell activation and release of preformed mediators.
Treatment with prednisolone resolved the allergic symptoms following subcutaneous ketamine administration.
Peak CCL3 (chemokine C-C motif ligand 3) concentration was significantly elevated 29-fold above baseline during a severe mast cell activation event.
IL-1ra concentration was significantly elevated 99-fold above baseline during a severe mast cell activation event.
IL-5 concentration was significantly elevated 44-fold above baseline during a severe mast cell activation event.
IL-6 concentration was significantly elevated 280-fold above baseline during a severe mast cell activation event, the largest fold-change observed among all cytokines measured.
IL-10 concentration was significantly elevated 93-fold above baseline during a severe mast cell activation event.
IL-13 concentration was significantly elevated 7-fold above baseline during a severe mast cell activation event.
Granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor was significantly elevated approximately 6-fold above baseline during the severe mast cell activation event.
During the moderate MCA event with confirmed influenza A infection, IFN-alpha was significantly elevated 5- to 7-fold above baseline, a smaller rise than the TH2 cytokines seen in severe events.
IFN-gamma was significantly elevated 5- to 7-fold above baseline during the moderate MCA event associated with influenza A infection.
TNF-alpha was significantly elevated 5- to 7-fold above baseline during the moderate MCA event associated with influenza A infection, a much smaller rise than TH2 cytokines during severe events.
Highly elevated histamine concentrations correlated with elevated cytokine concentrations during the acute phase at over 95%, suggesting a shared cellular source, likely activated mast cells.
The massive release of TH2 cytokines during the severe mast cell activation event induced a hyperinflammatory state that met published criteria for cytokine release syndrome.
The authors propose that administration of IL-6-inhibiting biologicals might significantly shorten the acute phase of severe mast cell activation events.
The authors propose that administration of IL-5-inhibiting biologicals might significantly shorten the acute phase of severe mast cell activation events.
A distinct single-cell cluster (cluster A) with a mast cell gene signature (TPSAB1, TPSB2, HDC) also co-expressed all three genes encoding the FcεRI subunits.
Mast cell progenitor cluster A cells retained residual/lower CD34 expression compared with the bulk CD34+ progenitor population, indicating an immature phenotype.

Pseudotime correlation analysis identified a population A gene signature encompassing protease, granule, FcεRI, KIT, activation, and prostaglandin-pathway genes that increase along the mast cell differentiation trajectory.
Nine of fourteen previously defined mature mast cell genes were represented within the population A progenitor signature, supporting a mast cell identity for these progenitors.

FCER1A was expressed in progenitors preceding the population A stage, while FCER1G (required for surface FcεRI expression) was upregulated together with mast cell genes specifically in population A, coinciding with surface FcεRI expression, indicating FcεRI can appear at the progenitor stage.
Sorted FcεRI+ population A progenitors progressed into c-Kithi mast cells more rapidly than FcεRI− progenitors during long-term culture.
Crosslinking FcεRI with IgE/anti-IgE on progenitor-derived mast cells caused upregulation of the activation marker CD63, confirming functional mast cell identity.

Population A (FcεRI+) progenitors isolated from three patients with systemic mastocytosis gave rise to mast cells after long-term culture, similar to healthy control-derived progenitors, indicating FcεRI+ progenitors are a potential mast cell source in this disease.
Mast cell progenitors expressed IL3RA, IL5RA, CSF2RB, EPOR, and notably IL1RL1 (IL-33 receptor), but showed low/undetectable CSF2RA, MPL, and FLT3.
IL-3 treatment induced strong, concentration-dependent proliferation of primary mast cell progenitors, serving as a robust reference condition for maintaining c-Kithi FcεRI+ cells.

IL-5, unlike IL-3, failed to induce robust mast cell progenitor proliferation even at concentrations up to 100 ng/mL, but it maintained the c-Kithi FcεRI+ population above background, suggesting a survival- rather than proliferation-promoting role.

IL-33 strongly downregulated FcεRI expression on primary mast cell progenitors, both in bulk c-Kit+ cultures and in FACS-isolated mast cell progenitors, an effect not seen with IL-5, GM-CSF, EPO, thrombopoietin, or Flt3L.
Unlike IL-33, cytokines IL-5, GM-CSF, EPO, thrombopoietin, and Flt3L failed to modulate FcεRI expression on mast cell progenitors after 5-day culture.

Cyp2c70-deficient mice, which have a human-like bile acid composition lacking hydrophilic muricholic acids, have previously been shown to develop cholangiopathy and biliary fibrosis with a female preponderance that is reversed by ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA).
Dietary OCA was incorporated into the biliary bile acid pool at 1-5%, with a greater enrichment in Cyp2c70-/- mice than in WT mice.
In wild-type mice, OCA treatment induced a more hydrophilic, muricholic-acid-rich bile acid pool.
In Cyp2c70-/- mice, OCA treatment made the bile acid pool more hydrophobic with a larger proportion of chenodeoxycholic acid, attributed to reduced bile acid 12alpha-hydroxylation.
OCA treatment reduced fecal bile acid excretion in both WT and Cyp2c70-/- mice, indicating repression of hepatic bile acid synthesis.
OCA treatment did not affect plasma markers of liver (dys)function in Cyp2c70-/- mice.
OCA treatment did not ameliorate or worsen cholangiopathy and biliary fibrosis in either male or female Cyp2c70-/- mice.
Prior work cited by the authors reported that ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) treatment reverses the cholangiopathy and biliary fibrosis seen in Cyp2c70-deficient mice.

Obeticholic acid, a steroidal FXR agonist, has been shown to improve liver function in patients with primary biliary cholangitis and is approved as a second-line treatment for those with inadequate response or intolerance to UDCA.
In a 58-year-old woman with clinically probable small fiber neuropathy and normal electroneuromyography, pain-related nociceptive evoked potential testing showed a delayed N1 latency.
The skin wrinkle test in the same patient showed a Grade 0 pattern (absence of water-induced wrinkling), consistent with sympathetic autonomic small fiber dysfunction.
Standard electroneuromyography was normal in this patient despite clinically probable small fiber neuropathy, highlighting the need for additional specialized testing.
In the initial MRN examination, microlesions vastly outnumbered intermediate and macrolesions along the L5/S1 root and sciatic, tibial and peroneal nerves (946 vs. 65 vs. 17 total lesions).
At the proximal thigh level, microlesion count was significantly higher than intermediate or macrolesion counts.
At the mid-thigh level, microlesion count was significantly higher than intermediate or macrolesion counts.
At the distal thigh level, microlesion count was significantly higher than intermediate or macrolesion counts.
At the pelvic and proximal calf levels, no significant difference was found between microlesion, intermediate lesion and macrolesion counts.
Total nerve lesion count was significantly higher at the proximal, mid- and distal thigh levels compared to the proximal calf level, with no significant differences among the thigh levels themselves.
Microlesion count did not differ significantly between initial and follow-up MRN examinations in nine patients over up to 71 months.
Intermediate lesion count did not differ significantly between initial and follow-up MRN examinations.
Macrolesion count did not differ significantly between initial and follow-up MRN examinations.
The diameter of microlesions decreased significantly at long-term follow-up compared to the initial examination.
The diameter of intermediate lesions did not differ significantly at long-term follow-up.
The diameter of macrolesions increased significantly at long-term follow-up, indicating progressive growth despite stable lesion number.

The spatial distribution of nerve lesions in schwannomatosis peaks at the mid-thigh level with a decrease toward the distal segments, which is markedly different from the proximal-to-distal increasing gradient described for NF2.

The proximal-to-distal spatial gradient of nerve lesions observed in schwannomatosis resembles the lesion distribution pattern described in diabetic and Fabry neuropathy, other length-dependent small fiber neuropathies.

Diagnosis of schwannomatosis in this cohort was confirmed by revised consensus clinical criteria together with genetic analysis of the NF2, SMARCB1 and LZTR1 genes in blood and, when available, tumor tissue.
Among 550 patients with IgM monoclonal gammopathy, 83 (15%) had an associated peripheral neuropathy.
Anti-MAG antibodies were detected in 38 of the 83 IgM-neuropathy patients, who showed heterogeneous clinical and neurophysiological features.
Four patients developed neurolymphomatosis presenting as a non-length dependent, predominantly motor neuropathy occurring long after IgM-MG diagnosis, which responded to hematological treatment.
Five patients had AL amyloid neuropathy that was revealed by a small fiber neuropathy presentation.

Thirty patients were classified as 'Neuropathy of Uncertain Relationship with the IgM' (NURIM), sharing clinical features with anti-MAG neuropathy at diagnosis but differing by a predominantly axonal neurophysiological pattern.
LTBP1 promotes the incorporation of fibrillin-1 and fibrillin-2 into the extracellular matrix in an in vitro model.
The short and long LTBP1 isoforms differentially exert the function of promoting fibrillin incorporation into the extracellular matrix.
Patients carrying LTBP1 pathogenic variants have been described with a wide spectrum of phenotypes across multiple tissues, suggesting a multifaceted role for LTBP1 in connective tissue homeostasis.
The study uncovers a novel TGFβ-independent function of LTBP1 in extracellular matrix formation that may contribute to the development of connective tissue disorders.
Circulating LPS levels are increased in high-fat-diet rodent models and in people with diarrhea-predominant IBS.
TLR2 agonists promoted neurogenesis and restored myenteric neurons in the colon of germ-free mice and antibiotic-depleted mice.
Germ-free mice and mice with enteric-neuron-specific Ahr deletion showed similarly reduced intestinal transit time compared to specific-pathogen-free and Ahr-expressing controls.
Serotonin signaling regulated by gut bacteria is disrupted in germ-free mice, obesity models, and IBS patients.
A 5-HT4 receptor agonist restored enteric nervous system innervation and intestinal transit time in germ-free mice, demonstrating its role in enteric neuron survival.
A GABA-producing probiotic reduced spinal neuron excitability in a rat model of visceral hypersensitivity, whereas a Bifidobacterium strain lacking GABA-producing enzymes failed to do so.
Fecal microbiota transplantation from lean donors dramatically increased circulating GABA levels in individuals with metabolic syndrome, potentially improving insulin sensitivity.
Bile acids reduce food intake dependent on TGR5 expression in vagal afferent neurons, with TGR5 and CCK synergistically activating nodose neurons.
Lack of FFAR3 signaling in utero, normally driven by maternal SCFA production, predisposed mice to high-fat-diet-induced obesity and metabolic syndrome via reduced energy expenditure.
Using a vagal-specific FFAR3 knockout mouse model, the authors found that vagal FFAR3 signaling regulates short-term feeding behavior in adults.
Increased colonic levels of Substance P have been observed after antibiotic treatment and in colitis models.
Probiotic supplementation with Dysosmobacter welbionis induced weight loss in mice, likely via activation of brown adipose thermogenesis.
A membrane protein from Akkermansia muciniphila that activates TLR2 was found responsible for its metabolic benefits, meaning viable bacteria were not required for the effect.
A case report described a diabetic woman whose glucose levels and pain indices improved after receiving FMT from a healthy donor.
FMT from lean donor mice to obese recipient mice improved peripheral hypersensitivity caused by a western diet, independent of glucose lowering or weight loss.
Antibiotic-induced visceral hypersensitivity in animal models can be prevented by probiotic supplementation with Lactobacillus.
Several Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium probiotics show promise for treating visceral pain in humans.
The prebiotic inulin improves constipation in people with IBS but can cause gas; combining it with the prebiotic psyllium counteracted this side effect.
FMT improved patient outcomes in several IBS trials but worsened symptoms in other studies, indicating heterogeneous efficacy.
Reduced bacterial diversity, richness, and stability are often reported in both obesity and IBS.
There are conflicting findings on whether Prevotella species are expanded in IBS patients.
Antibiotic-treated mice show reduced enteric neuron innervation and disrupted excitability, contributing to slowed intestinal transit and reduced motility.
Modified Rodnan's skin score (mRSS), a clinical marker of skin fibrosis, decreased significantly from baseline to 12 months after AHSCT.
Histological skin thickness measured on H&E-stained biopsies decreased significantly after AHSCT compared to baseline.
Collagen density measured by picrosirius red staining decreased significantly in skin biopsies after AHSCT.
Cutaneous immunohistochemical expression of MMP-1 did not change after AHSCT compared to baseline.
Cutaneous expression of MMP-2 increased significantly after AHSCT.
Cutaneous expression of MMP-3 increased significantly after AHSCT.
Cutaneous expression of MMP-9 increased significantly after AHSCT.
Cutaneous expression of TIMP-1 increased significantly after AHSCT, correlating with mRSS changes.
Cutaneous NF-κB p65 expression decreased significantly after AHSCT, suggesting reduced inflammatory-fibrotic signaling.
Skin expression of the myofibroblast marker α-SMA did not change after AHSCT.
Skin expression of the profibrotic cytokine TGF-β did not change significantly after AHSCT.
Serum S100A9 concentrations were significantly higher in SSc patients at baseline compared to healthy controls.
Serum S100A9 levels decreased and normalized to healthy control levels after AHSCT, correlating with mRSS improvement.
Serum COL4A1 remained significantly higher than healthy controls both before and after AHSCT, suggesting persistent vasculopathy despite fibrosis improvement.
Serum PDGF-AA levels were significantly lower in SSc patients than healthy controls at baseline and remained lower, decreasing further after AHSCT.
Serum PDGF-BB levels were significantly lower in SSc patients than healthy controls at baseline and remained lower, decreasing further after AHSCT.
Serum TIMP-1 concentrations decreased significantly in SSc patients after AHSCT.
Serum COL1A1 levels increased significantly after AHSCT and became higher than in healthy controls, and this increase negatively correlated with mRSS improvement.
Serum MMP-1 concentrations decreased significantly after AHSCT, and this decrease strongly correlated with mRSS improvement, despite MMP-1 skin expression not correlating with these changes.
Serum levels of MMP-3, MMP-12, MMP-13, and FGF-1 did not change after AHSCT and were not different from healthy controls.
Cutaneous MMP-3 expression correlated with baseline mRSS severity.
Cutaneous MMP-1 expression correlated positively with baseline mRSS severity.
Changes in skin collagen density correlated positively with changes in mRSS after AHSCT.
Changes in serum PDGF-AA and PDGF-BB after AHSCT correlated positively with changes in mRSS.
At baseline, patients with more severe skin involvement (mRSS>20) had higher serum COL4A1 and PDGF-BB than those with mRSS≤20.
After AHSCT, serum MMP-3, MMP-12, and FGF-1 were higher in patients with more severe baseline skin involvement (mRSS>20) than in mRSS≤20 patients.
