6-OAP abrogated anti-IgE-induced intracellular calcium influx/mobilization in HCMC.
6-OAP inhibited anti-IgE-induced phosphorylation of ERK in HCMC as shown by Western blot.
RNA-seq/GO/KEGG analysis showed that 6-OAP up-regulated expression of SCF complex-related genes, particularly ubiquitin ligase-associated genes, in HCMC.

Nano-SiO2 particles (20 nm) at 100 µg/mL significantly increased β-hexosaminidase release from IgE-sensitized mast cells stimulated with DNP-HSA, compared with DNP-HSA stimulation alone, indicating synergistic mast cell activation.

In the non-IgE pathway, SiO2 (20 nm and 2.34 µm), Al2O3 (26.93 µm), and Fe2O3 (50 nm and 1 µm) produced statistically significant but slight stimulatory effects on mast cell degranulation at 100 µg/mL.
Both 50 nm and 1 µm Fe2O3 particles exhibited strong, dose-dependent cytotoxicity to bone marrow-derived mast cells.
Nano-SiO2 particles significantly increased Evan's blue dye extravasation and ear thickness in the IgE-mediated passive cutaneous anaphylaxis (PCA) mouse model compared with DNP-HSA alone.
Airway resistance (Rrs) was significantly higher in OVA+SiO2 mice than in OVA-alone mice after methacholine challenge, indicating that nano-SiO2 exposure exacerbates airway hyperresponsiveness.
Serum OVA-specific IgE levels were significantly higher in OVA+SiO2 mice than OVA-alone mice, though this trend was not observed in BALF.
Total inflammatory cell counts in BALF were significantly higher in nano-SiO2-exposed allergic asthma mice than in blank and OVA-alone groups.
Nano-SiO2 exposure significantly increased IL-4 and IL-6 in BALF of OVA+SiO2 mice compared with OVA alone, and IL-4 (but not IL-6) was elevated by SiO2 exposure alone versus blank control.
Histamine levels in serum and BALF were increased after nano-SiO2 exposure compared with blank control, and significantly higher in OVA+SiO2 than OVA alone mice.
Nano-SiO2 exposure did not significantly change serum/BALF tryptase levels, with no difference between OVA alone and OVA+SiO2 groups.

OVA+SiO2 exposure induced more severe lung histopathological injury, higher mucus hypersecretion (PAS) scores, and greater aggregation of mast cell tryptase-positive cells in lung tissue than OVA alone.

STXM dual-energy imaging and TEM demonstrated that nano-SiO2 particles were internalized by mast cells, with cell-covered regions showing an approximately doubled frequency of silicon signal compared to background.

TEM showed no clear morphological degranulation in mast cells treated with SiO2 alone, whereas DNP-HSA+SiO2 co-treatment produced increased intracellular vacuolization compared with DNP-HSA alone, consistent with enhanced degranulation.
Transcriptome sequencing of nano-SiO2-treated mast cells identified 285 significantly differentially expressed genes, 135 of which were linked to oxidative stress via GeneCards database annotation.

KEGG pathway enrichment analysis of differentially expressed genes in nano-SiO2-treated mast cells showed enrichment in cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction, NF-κB signaling, and MAPK signaling pathways.
Nano-SiO2 exposure significantly upregulated MAPK-pathway-related genes including Areg, Ptgs2, Tnf, Hspa1a, Map3k8, Malt1, Ccl3, Ccl4, and Il6 in mast cells.
Nano-SiO2 exposure did not significantly alter FcϵRI receptor expression or IgE-binding capacity on mast cells, whether unsensitized or IgE-sensitized.

Western blotting showed nano-SiO2 treatment increased phosphorylated ERK1/2 in DNP-HSA-stimulated mast cells beyond DNP-HSA stimulation alone, implicating enhanced MAPK/ERK signaling in the synergistic activation.
Nano-SiO2 treatment alone increased phospho-p38 expression relative to blank control, but this increase was not observed in combination with DNP-HSA stimulation.
NF-κB, phospho-Plcγ1, and phospho-JNK were upregulated following mast cell activation, but nano-SiO2 co-treatment did not further increase these markers compared with DNP-HSA stimulation alone.

Pretreatment with ERK inhibitor U0126-EtOH or p38 inhibitor SB203580 significantly reduced β-hexosaminidase release in SiO2, DNP-HSA, and DNP-HSA+SiO2 groups, with the ERK inhibitor showing a greater effect than the p38 inhibitor, supporting a role for MAPK/ERK signaling in nano-SiO2's synergistic mast cell activation.

Transcriptomic analysis identified significant changes in MAPK-pathway-related genes Gadd45b and Nr4a1 in nano-SiO2-treated mast cells, genes previously implicated in FcϵRI-stimulated mast cell activation and oxidative-stress-related JNK signaling.
Western blotting showed that nano-SiO2 particle treatment increased phosphorylated ERK1/2 expression in IgE-sensitized, DNP-HSA-stimulated mast cells compared with DNP-HSA stimulation alone.
Nano-SiO2 exposure alone increased phosphorylated p38 expression compared with blank control, but this increase was not observed after DNP-HSA stimulation.
NF-κB, phospho-Plcγ1 and phospho-JNK were upregulated upon mast cell activation, but no significant differences were seen between DNP-HSA stimulation alone and DNP-HSA plus nano-SiO2.
Nano-SiO2 exposure did not significantly change surface FcϵRI expression on unsensitized mast cells compared with blank control.
In IgE-sensitized mast cells, nano-SiO2 treatment did not significantly alter FcϵRI expression or IgE binding capacity compared with blank control.

Pretreatment with the ERK inhibitor U0126-EtOH (5 μM/L) or the p38 inhibitor SB203580 (10 μM/L) significantly reduced β-hexosaminidase release in SiO2, DNP-HSA, and DNP-HSA+SiO2 groups, with the ERK inhibitor showing a stronger effect (reducing release by about 10-25%).
Transcriptome cluster analysis of MAPK/NF-κB/ERK1/2-related genes showed nano-SiO2 exposure significantly upregulated Areg, Ptgs2, Tnf, Hspa1a, Map3k8, Malt1, Ccl3, Ccl4, and Il6 in mast cells.
At low concentrations (25 and 50 μg/mL), none of the tested particles (Al2O3, TiO2, Fe2O3, SiO2) significantly activated mast cells with or without DNP-HSA stimulation.
Only 20 nm SiO2 particles, and not Al2O3, TiO2, Fe2O3, or larger 2.34 μm SiO2, were able to synergistically increase β-hexosaminidase release from IgE-sensitized, DNP-HSA-stimulated mast cells.

Among MAPK-pathway genes altered by nano-SiO2 in the transcriptome data, Nr4a1 was noted, a gene previously reported to promote FcϵRI-stimulated mast cell activation and anaphylaxis by counteracting the inhibitory LKB1/AMPK axis.

Gadd45b, an environmental-stress-responsive gene altered in the nano-SiO2 transcriptome data, has been reported elsewhere to mediate PM2.5-promoted IgE-mediated mast cell activation via the ROS/Gadd45b/JNK axis.

In the authors' previous work, none of nine water-soluble inorganic salts activated mast cells via IgE or non-IgE pathways, and only malonic acid among three organic acids showed a very weak activation effect.
Reducing intake of fermentable carbohydrates improved abdominal pain in patients with IBS and was accompanied by changes in gut microbiota and decreased urinary histamine.
Germ-free mice colonized with fecal microbiota from IBS patients with high, but not low, urinary histamine developed visceral hyperalgesia and mast cell activation.
Feeding colonized germ-free mice a diet with reduced fermentable carbohydrates decreased visceral hypersensitivity and mast cell accumulation in the colon.
Fecal microbiota from IBS patients with high, but not low, urinary histamine produced large amounts of histamine in vitro.
Klebsiella aerogenes carrying a histidine decarboxylase gene variant was identified as a major producer of the histamine detected in high-histamine IBS fecal microbiota.
This histamine-producing Klebsiella aerogenes strain was highly abundant in the fecal microbiota of three independent cohorts of IBS patients compared with healthy individuals.

Pharmacological blockade of the histamine 4 receptor in vivo inhibited visceral hypersensitivity and decreased colonic mast cell accumulation in germ-free mice colonized with high histamine-producing IBS fecal microbiota.
The total number of circulating extracellular vesicles did not differ significantly between chronic urticaria patients and healthy controls.
Levels of CD3+ (T-cell) extracellular vesicles were significantly decreased in chronic urticaria patients compared with healthy controls.
Levels of CD146+ (endothelial cell) extracellular vesicles were significantly decreased in chronic urticaria patients compared with healthy controls.
No significant differences were observed in platelet-derived extracellular vesicles between chronic urticaria patients and healthy controls.
No significant differences were observed in macrophage-derived extracellular vesicles between chronic urticaria patients and healthy controls.
No significant differences were observed in PECAM-1-positive extracellular vesicles between chronic urticaria patients and healthy controls.
No significant differences were observed in B cell-derived extracellular vesicles between chronic urticaria patients and healthy controls.
No significant differences were observed in tissue factor-positive extracellular vesicles between chronic urticaria patients and healthy controls.
A gain-of-function IL-4Rα Y709F mutation in IL9Tg mice altered the clinical symptoms produced by a single oral egg antigen exposure compared to IL9Tg mice without the mutation.
Mice with enhanced IL-4Rα signaling (Y709F) tolerated a lower cumulative antigen dose before reacting during oral food challenge compared to mice without the mutation.
Enhanced IL-4Rα signaling increased the severity of allergic reactions during oral food challenge and altered the frequency of adverse events and outcomes during oral immunotherapy (OIT).

Biomarkers measured after the first oral antigen exposure, including mast cell activation and ovalbumin-specific IgE levels, were assessed for their ability to predict reactivity during food challenge and OIT, but only initial reaction severity significantly correlated with cumulative dose tolerated during oral food challenge.

Skin sensitization followed by a single intragastric egg antigen exposure in intestinal IL-9 transgenic (IL9Tg) mice, with or without the IL-4Rα Y709F mutation, was sufficient to induce a food allergic reaction, establishing a murine model of food allergy diagnosis and treatment.
A patient developed small-fiber neuropathy and tinnitus following COVID-19 vaccination, which was treated with plasma exchange.
A woman with PCR-confirmed Angiostrongylus cantonensis infection presented with small fiber neuropathy symptoms but no headache, an atypical presentation for this parasite.
Small fiber neuropathy was confirmed via skin biopsy in this patient.
After failing standard neuropathy medications, the patient improved considerably with intravenous lidocaine treatment.
Standard medications for neuropathy failed to adequately control the patient's symptoms prior to lidocaine treatment.
The patient required ongoing medication for one year to manage chronic neuropathy stemming from the infection, indicating a persistent long-term sequela.
Mutations in the FBN1 gene, which encodes fibrillin-1, were established as the cause of Marfan syndrome.
Prophylactic treatment with sartans in combination with beta-blockers may reduce or delay the development of aortic root aneurysm in Marfan syndrome.

Neutralizing AP-1 with decoy oligodeoxynucleotide (dODN) technology significantly reduced aortic elastolysis, macrophage infiltration, and MMP activity in an established Marfan mouse aortic graft model.

AAV-mediated expression of an RNA hairpin decoy oligonucleotide against AP-1 restored ZO-1 tight junction protein levels and reduced MMP expression/activity, reactive oxygen species, monocyte chemoattractant protein-1, and monocyte infiltration while preserving elastin architecture in Marfan mouse aortic grafts.

AAV-delivered AP-1 TFD treatment significantly decreased TGF-beta concentration and downstream signalling in cultured human aortic smooth muscle cells from Marfan patients, an effect comparable to a TGF-beta neutralizing antibody.

A porcine Marfan syndrome model carrying a heterozygous FBN1 mutation (+/Glu433AsnfsX98), generated via genome editing and somatic cell nuclear transfer, reproduced classical MFS features including scoliosis, reduced bone density, and aortic elastic fibre fragmentation.

miR-29b was identified as a critical regulator of aortic wall apoptosis and extracellular matrix abnormalities in early thoracic aneurysm development in Marfan syndrome, but its suppression is only protective when applied prenatally and does not affect already-established aneurysms.
Resveratrol has been established as a drug that downregulates miR-29b, though no clinical investigation of this effect in Marfan patients exists yet.
Overexpression of the extracellular matrix marker PAI-1 prevented the development of abdominal aortic aneurysms in mice, but this approach was not pursued in further research.
Adenovirus-mediated overexpression of TIMP-1 in a murine heterotopic aortic transplant model (mgR/mgR mice) led to massive intimal hyperplasia in the Marfan aorta.

When delivered by apathogenic AAV rather than adenovirus, TIMP-1 overexpression significantly reduced MMP9 activity in the heterotopic aortic transplant model without the intimal hyperplasia seen with adenoviral delivery.
Adenovirus-mediated overexpression of tropoelastin induced production of healthy elastin fibres and proved helpful in a rat model, but this approach was not pursued in clinical research.

In-frame FBN1 mutations altering cysteine content show differential clinical impact: cysteine loss variants show overall higher severity and aortic risk, while cysteine addition variants have the highest frequency of ectopia lentis surgery.
FBN1 mutations resulting in haploinsufficiency were associated with more cases of aortic dissection occurring at a younger age compared with other mutation types.
CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing was used to successfully target and eliminate the FBN1 T7498C mutation in human embryos, with no modification found in the previously affected allele on testing.
Valve-sparing aortic root replacement surgery for Marfan syndrome can now be performed with less than 1% operative mortality in specialized centres.

Histological analysis of a single Marfan syndrome patient who underwent Personalized External Aortic Root Support (PEARS) showed complete incorporation of the microporous mesh into the aortic adventitia.

The authors' working group demonstrated transadventitial uptake of AAV-mediated EGFP delivery into aortic smooth muscle and endothelial cells using an SMC- and endothelial cell-specific AAV, without adverse reactions affecting other solid organs.

The aorta of Marfan mice showed loss of tight junction proteins ZO-1 and occludin, increasing endothelial monolayer permeability and enabling transcription factor decoy oligonucleotide penetration into the tunica media.
Serum TGF-β1 levels on day 1 were significantly higher in COVID-19 patients than in healthy controls.
Serum TGF-β1 levels on day 7 were significantly higher in COVID-19 patients than in controls and higher than the patients' own day 1 levels, despite improvement in routine inflammatory markers.
Serum CTGF levels on day 1 were significantly higher in COVID-19 patients than in healthy controls.
Serum CTGF levels on day 7 rose further compared to day 1 and remained significantly higher than controls, tracking ongoing lung repair/fibrotic processes despite normalization of routine labs.
Serum TGF-β1 and CTGF levels were strongly, positively correlated with one another in COVID-19 patients.
Serum TGF-β1 and CTGF levels correlated with clinical severity of COVID-19, with the critical patient group showing the highest levels on both day 1 and day 7.
Day 1 serum TGF-β1 levels did not significantly differ among moderate, severe, and critical pneumonia subgroups, though day 7 levels did differ significantly.
Serum TGF-β1 levels were moderately and positively correlated with D-dimer, ESR, ferritin, CRP, and LDH in COVID-19 patients.
Serum CTGF levels were moderately and positively correlated with D-dimer, ESR, ferritin, CRP, and LDH in COVID-19 patients.
ROC analysis showed serum CTGF had good diagnostic accuracy for distinguishing COVID-19 lung injury on day 1 and excellent accuracy on day 7.
ROC analysis showed serum TGF-β1 had poor-to-modest diagnostic accuracy on day 1 but excellent accuracy on day 7 for distinguishing COVID-19 lung injury.

On day 1, routine inflammatory and injury markers (LDH, D-dimer, troponin-I, ESR, CRP, ferritin) were significantly higher in COVID-19 patients than controls, but normalized to control levels by day 7 despite ongoing TGF-β1/CTGF elevation.
White blood cell, neutrophil, and lymphocyte counts were significantly lower in COVID-19 patients than controls on day 1, normalizing by day 7.
In the right lateral decubitus position, diabetic patients had a significantly larger antral cross-sectional area than non-diabetic patients.
Calculated residual gastric volume in the right lateral decubitus position was significantly higher in diabetic patients than in non-diabetic patients.
Directly measured gastric tube aspirate volume after induction of anesthesia was significantly higher in diabetic patients than in non-diabetic patients.
A significantly greater proportion of diabetic patients had grade 1 antral fluid (fluid visible in RLD only) compared with non-diabetic patients, who mostly had an empty (grade 0) antrum.
In the semi-sitting position, diabetic patients had a significantly larger antral cross-sectional area than non-diabetic patients.
Despite higher antral volumes in diabetics, no patient in either group met the high-risk threshold (>1.5 ml/kg) for pulmonary aspiration.
The paper attributes delayed gastric emptying and increased full-stomach risk in diabetic patients to autonomic gastropathy and gastroduodenal motor abnormalities.
Orthostatic hypotension is estimated to affect 40% of Parkinson's disease patients, causing dizziness, syncope, and increased fall risk.
Approximately 80% of Parkinson's disease patients present abnormalities in heart rate and blood pressure.
Patients with PD show reduced heart rate variability (HRV) with lower LF values compared to healthy controls, alongside attenuated sympathetic activity.
PD patients show loss of sympathetic noradrenergic nerves in the heart and kidneys.

In male rats, bilateral 6-OHDA lesion of the SNpc decreases baseline mean arterial pressure and heart rate, with reduced systolic blood pressure modulation and altered baroreflex/chemoreflex responses.

Bilateral 6-OHDA lesion reduced the night/day heart rate cycle change and weakened phenylephrine-induced bradycardia in rats, and decreased response to alpha-adrenergic blockade suggesting impaired sympathetic vascular synaptic transmission.

Bilateral 6-OHDA and Prolopa-treated rats showed lower cardiovascular compensation during head-up tilt, indicating autonomic impairment in 6-OHDA-induced parkinsonism, along with lower baroreflex sensitivity and fewer brainstem cardiovascular neurons.

In the MPTP mouse model, attenuation of baroreflex sensitivity was associated with loss of TH+ neurons and decreased brainstem catecholamines, along with increased heart rate, decreased HRV power, increased sympathetic tone and decreased parasympathetic tone.
Non-specific NOS inhibitor L-NAME reduced the neurodegenerative response following 6-OHDA injury in rats.
In the MPTP model, the nNOS inhibitor 7-Nitroindazole and the iNOS inhibitor S-methylisothiourea were effective in protecting against MPTP neurotoxic effects.
Selective iNOS inhibitor GW274150 significantly attenuated dopamine loss in the striatum after unilateral 6-OHDA injury in Sprague-Dawley rats.
Increased dopaminergic neurodegeneration in 6-OHDA-injured rats is associated with decreased nNOS concentration in the substantia nigra, whereas MPTP injury in mice increases iNOS.
MPTP toxicity differs by sex, with males showing faster dopamine decrease and earlier increased striatal expression of iNOS and nNOS, while females show better recovery.
Genetic variants in the genes responsible for iNOS and nNOS are correlated with the risk of developing Parkinson's disease.
Plasma nitric oxide concentration is decreased in patients with Parkinson's disease without a corresponding decrease in NOS activity.

Nitrite concentration in the aorta was increased in 6-OHDA-injured rats compared to controls, and L-NAME produced a smaller increase in MAP in 6-OHDA animals, suggesting lower eNOS nitrergic tone after 6-OHDA injury.

Adult female rats do not show the cardiovascular dysfunction (hypotension) seen in males with 6-OHDA parkinsonism, but ovariectomized females develop basal hypotension and higher aortic nitrite concentration, suggesting an ovarian hormone-linked role for NO at the vascular level.
nNOS is increased in the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus in male 6-OHDA injured rats, increasing GABAergic tone on cardiovascular function and contributing to lower basal blood pressure.
Diabetic neuropathy and hormonal disruption can cause upper and/or lower gastrointestinal symptoms in up to 75% of diabetic patients, affecting multiple GI organs.

Altered gastrointestinal motility and/or secretions can in turn affect glucose and lipid homeostasis over the short and long term, indicating a bidirectional relationship between GI function and metabolic control.
Diabetes has been linked with an increased risk of cancer at different levels of the gastrointestinal tract.
A higher n-6/n-3 PUFA ratio was associated with a greater number of overlapping nociplastic pain conditions.
Higher circulating omega-6 linoleic acid was negatively associated with pressure pain thresholds at three of six anatomical sites, indicating greater pain sensitivity.
Higher circulating omega-6 arachidonic acid was negatively associated with pressure pain thresholds at five of six anatomical sites, indicating greater pain sensitivity.
Circulating omega-3 alpha-linolenic acid was not significantly associated with nociceptive thresholds at any of the six anatomical sites tested.
Circulating omega-3 eicosapentaenoic acid was not significantly associated with nociceptive thresholds at any of the six anatomical sites tested.
Circulating omega-3 docosahexaenoic acid was not significantly associated with nociceptive thresholds at any of the six anatomical sites tested.
The n-6/n-3 PUFA ratio was not associated with nociceptive pressure pain thresholds at any of the six anatomical sites tested.

Participants with nociplastic pain conditions (including irritable bowel syndrome, fibromyalgia, TMD, headache, low back pain) had significantly lower nociceptive pressure pain thresholds than non-case controls at all six anatomical sites examined.
Treatment of human primary osteoblasts with mast cell chymase caused pronounced morphological changes, including extensive cell contraction and reorganization of the actin cytoskeleton.
Chymase caused a profound reduction in the output of collagen from human osteoblasts.
Chymase was shown to degrade osteoblast-secreted fibronectin.
Chymase was shown to activate pro-matrix metallopeptidase-2 (pro-MMP-2) released by osteoblasts.
Chymase preferentially altered the gene expression, protein output, and phosphorylation status of TGFβ-associated signaling molecules in osteoblasts.
A transcriptomic analysis showed chymase significantly affected several bone metabolism genes, including a reduction in osteoprotegerin expression, which was confirmed at the protein level.
Chymase was shown to interact with human osteoblasts and to be taken up by the cells.
Chymase treatment reduced the expression of osteoprotegerin in human osteoblasts, a finding confirmed at the protein level.
Chymase was shown to physically interact with human osteoblasts and to be internalized (taken up) by these cells.
CD44 expression in the uterosacral ligament was significantly lower in women with pelvic organ prolapse compared with women without prolapse.
MMP-2 expression in the uterosacral ligament was significantly higher in women with pelvic organ prolapse compared with women without prolapse.
MMP-9 expression in the uterosacral ligament was significantly higher in women with pelvic organ prolapse compared with women without prolapse.
TGF-β expression in the uterosacral ligament did not differ significantly between women with and without pelvic organ prolapse.
CD44 expression was negatively correlated with the occurrence of pelvic organ prolapse in Spearman's correlation analysis.
MMP-2 expression was positively correlated with the occurrence of pelvic organ prolapse.
MMP-9 expression was positively correlated with the occurrence of pelvic organ prolapse.
Older age and longer postmenopausal duration were positively correlated with, and clinically associated with, occurrence of pelvic organ prolapse.
Women with pelvic organ prolapse showed a higher incidence of hypertension compared with women without prolapse.
CD44 expression did not differ significantly by age subgroup between POP and control patients (younger vs older).
MYOC mutations were identified in 3 of 8 (37.5%) autosomal dominant juvenile-onset open-angle glaucoma families.
LTBP2 mutation was identified in 1 of 8 (12.5%) autosomal dominant JOAG families.
A rare EFEMP1 sequence variant was found in one autosomal dominant JOAG family, present in both an affected father and daughter.
The daughter in the EFEMP1-variant family also carried a pathogenic COL11A1 sequence variant and had high myopia, leading to a coincidental diagnosis of Stickler syndrome.
The study reiterates that EFEMP1 should be considered a candidate gene in autosomal dominant juvenile-onset open-angle glaucoma families.
ACE2 expression across 49 GTEx tissues was highest in testis, small intestine, adipose, kidney cortex, and heart, with arterial and brain tissues also higher than most other tissues.
ACE2 expression showed sex differences in GTEx data, being higher in females than males in adipose-subcutaneous and whole blood, but lower in females than males in breast mammary tissue (all p<0.01).
The ACE2 promoter SNP rs2106809 minor allele G was associated with reduced risk of COVID-19 hospitalization in the European-ancestry UK Biobank GWAS.
The EUR-specific rare ACE2 SNP rs62578876 minor allele was associated with protection against COVID-19 hospitalization in the UK Biobank GWAS.
The intronic EUR-specific ACE2 SNP rs183546232 minor allele was associated with increased risk of COVID-19 hospitalization in the UK Biobank GWAS.
rs2106809 acts as a strong eQTL for ACE2 expression across multiple brain tissues as well as nerve and artery tissues in GTEx, with a marginal association in lung (p=0.07).

The association between rs2106809 and higher ACE2 expression across multiple brain tissues was replicated using the independent UK brain eQTL database Braineac, and overall the G allele was linked to both higher brain ACE2 expression and protection against COVID-19 hospitalization.

In dual luciferase reporter assays, the rs2106809 GG genotype increased ACE2 promoter activity compared to the AA genotype in HEK293T cells, and significantly enhanced promoter activity in A549 cells.
A multicenter clinical trial of 3,408 patients found the rs2106809 major allele A conferred a 1.6-fold increased risk of hypertension in Chinese women.
A study of 647 Chinese Han patients found the rs2106809 A allele was statistically associated with a 2.0-fold increased risk of left ventricular hypertrophy.
A study of 246 hypertensives and 274 normotensives from Odisha, India, reported a significant relationship between the rs2106809 polymorphism and essential hypertension.

A clinical survey of 96 Chinese female essential hypertension patients found circulating Ang(1-7) levels were significantly higher in patients carrying the rs2106809 G allele than those carrying the A allele.

A case study of 155 COVID-19 patients from Turkey found the ACE2 rs2106809 polymorphism was not associated with clinical severity of COVID-19 infection, contrasting with this paper's UK Biobank finding.
A Chinese epidemiological investigation found that 37.6% of hospitalized COVID-19 patients were subsequently diagnosed with long COVID.
A study from the Faroe Islands reported that around 50% of non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients developed long COVID.
At six-month follow-up, 83% of hospitalized COVID-19 survivors had at least one of ten standardized-scale-measured symptoms, with a median of two symptoms per patient.
Pain, fatigue, PTSD, and memory impairment were the most commonly reported symptoms at follow-up.
Objective testing found muscle strength impairment in almost two-thirds and pulmonary function abnormalities in one-third of patients at follow-up.
Female sex was associated with worse post-COVID-19 outcomes, including increased dyspnoea, lower functional status, increased fatigue, and higher anxiety/depression scores.
Younger age was associated with higher anxiety and depression scores at follow-up.
Lower socioeconomic position was associated with increased dyspnoea, increased fatigue, and worse functional status at follow-up.
A higher burden of comorbidities at hospital admission was associated with increased dyspnoea, increased fatigue, and lower functional status at follow-up.
Higher BMI was associated with increased dyspnoea at follow-up.
Intubation during hospitalization was unexpectedly associated with decreased fatigue and lower anxiety/depression scores at follow-up.
Longer hospital length of stay was associated with increased fatigue and worse functional status at follow-up.
Neighbourhood per capita income, population density, and individual greenspace exposure were not significantly associated with dyspnoea, fatigue, anxiety/depression, or functional status.
Higher ambient air pollution (PM2.5) exposure around a patient's residence was associated with increased dyspnoea, lower functional status, and increased fatigue at follow-up.
Smoking history and self-declared race were not significantly associated with the selected post-COVID-19 outcomes.

Study participants had higher BMI, more previous hypertension, and more severe acute disease (longer hospitalization, more ICU/intubation) than eligible patients who were excluded or did not participate, suggesting selection bias toward more severe cases.
Post-COVID-19 functional status, measured with the PCFS Scale, was abnormal in approximately one-third of participants at six-month follow-up.

Patients evaluated later after hospitalization (post-median 200 days) had a higher prevalence of anxiety, depression, dyspnoea, severe muscle/joint pain, and loss of smell at follow-up compared to those evaluated earlier.
Adolescents with ME/CFS reported that missing school due to illness caused significant stress, anxiety, and loss of social connections with peers.
Families held divergent views on whether inability to attend school was an early symptom of ME/CFS onset or whether school-related stress (e.g., exam pressure) contributed to the illness developing.
ME/CFS specialist clinicians observed that symptoms often improved once exam pressure (e.g., GCSEs) ended, suggesting school/exam stress exacerbates symptoms.

A managed, graded (part-time/phased) return to school with a consistent routine was described by adolescents, parents, and clinicians as helping recovery and avoiding relapse, whereas pushing full attendance too quickly was seen as unsustainable and could worsen symptoms.

Many families described difficulty accessing educational support and administrative failures (lost paperwork, unfulfilled promises of tutoring, being passed between authorities), which increased family stress and burden.
Some families reported being accused of truancy, fined, or threatened with prosecution by local authorities due to their child's poor school attendance resulting from ME/CFS.
Some families felt schools became more supportive and provided help once a formal ME/CFS diagnosis and medical evidence were received, particularly with input from the ME/CFS service.
Many families reported that providing medical evidence of ME/CFS did not increase educational support, as school staff sometimes disbelieved the illness because standard medical tests were normal.

Practical school-based strategies (rest/nurture rooms, exit passes, slower lesson pace, part-time timetables, exemption from PE) were described as helping adolescents manage ME/CFS symptoms and avoid 'boom and bust' fatigue cycles, especially when implemented by teachers with prior knowledge of ME/CFS.
Teachers with prior personal or professional experience of ME/CFS were associated with adolescents feeling more supported and understood at school.

Poor communication between schools, GPs, local authorities, and ME/CFS specialist services was identified by all participant groups as a barrier; a multi-way integrated communication model was proposed.

Background literature cited indicates young people with ME/CFS in specialist services attend a median of two days of school per week, with mean total time absent from school of approximately one year.
Cited literature indicates nearly 70% of young people with ME/CFS feel their illness significantly affects their future career plans.
Cited literature found that young people with ME/CFS have reduced academic performance compared to healthy peers.
TRPM3 ion channel current amplitude after PregS stimulation was significantly reduced in NK cells from ME/CFS patients compared with healthy controls.
TRPM3 ion channel current amplitude after PregS stimulation was significantly reduced in NK cells from post COVID-19 condition patients compared with healthy controls, mimicking the ME/CFS result.
There was no significant difference in TRPM3 ion channel current amplitude after PregS stimulation between ME/CFS and post COVID-19 condition patients.
NK cell ionic currents from ME/CFS patients were largely resistant to ononetin blockade in the presence of PregS, indicating significant loss of TRPM3 channel function compared with healthy controls.
NK cell ionic currents from post COVID-19 condition patients were also significantly resistant to ononetin compared with healthy controls, and this insensitivity was greater than in ME/CFS.

SF-36 quality of life scores differed significantly between HC, ME/CFS and post COVID-19 condition groups across multiple domains including physical functioning, physical role, pain, general health, social functioning and vitality.

WHO Disability Assessment Schedule (DAS) scores differed significantly between groups for communication and understanding, mobility, interpersonal relationships, participation in life activities and participation in society.

Routine full blood count parameters (red blood cell, white blood cell, granulocyte counts) were within normal range and showed no significant differences between HC, ME/CFS and post COVID-19 condition groups.
NK cell purity (CD3-CD56+) determined by flow cytometry did not significantly differ between HC, ME/CFS and post COVID-19 condition groups.

All ME/CFS and post COVID-19 condition patients reported cognitive difficulties and sleep disturbances; pain was reported in all ME/CFS and 80% of post COVID-19 condition patients; sensory and immune disturbances were reported in 80% of ME/CFS and all post COVID-19 condition patients.

Prior in vitro treatment with naltrexone hydrochloride restored TRPM3 ion channel function and re-established calcium homeostasis in NK cells from ME/CFS patients, and low dose naltrexone (3.0-5.0 mg/day) normalised TRPM3 activity in ME/CFS patients in a subsequent study.
CFS/ME patients show diminished natural killer (NK) lymphocyte activity as part of broader immune alterations.
Increased levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines may explain fatigue and flu-like symptoms in CFS/ME and may affect NK activity.
CFS/ME patients show an increased number of CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes with increased CD38 and HLA-DR activation markers.
CFS/ME patients show reduced CD11b expression associated with increased CD28+ T subset expression.

Freitag et al. reported that reactivity of autoantibodies against vasoregulative G-protein-coupled receptors correlates with autonomic dysfunction, clinical severity, and disability in CFS/ME patients.
Kujawski et al. studied post-exertional malaise (PEM) as an indicator linked to aortic stiffness, autonomic nervous system function, and fatigue severity in CFS/ME patients.

Van Oosterwijck et al. showed decreased parasympathetic reactivation following physical exercise in CFS/ME patients, potentially correlated with poor prognosis or higher risk for adverse cardiac events.
Varesi et al. investigated a modified composition of gut microbiota in CFS/ME individuals in relation to genetic, infectious, and immunological influences.
Baklund et al. evaluated blood test results in relation to clinical features and diagnostic classification, suggesting evidence of muscle damage and metabolic abnormalities in CFS/ME.

Castro-Marrero et al. examined complement C1 as a potential blood diagnostic tool across three CFS/ME symptom clusters (severe, moderate, mild), finding important differences in five blood parameters.
Lim et al. published a meta-analysis on the two-day cardiopulmonary exercise test (CPET) as an objective measurement to assess functional impairment and PEM, a hallmark of CFS/ME.
A systematic review by Kim et al. found that around 40% of RCTs in CFS/ME utilized multiple primary outcome measurements, informing future trial design.
Tirelli and colleagues compared oxygen-ozone autohemotherapy (O2-O3-AHT) responses between male and female CFS/ME patients, finding differences by sex.

Kujawski et al. found that a personalized structured activity program improved cardiovascular, mitochondrial, and fatigue parameters, showing a reduction in fatigue and improved functional performance in CFS/ME patients.
Scheibenbogen and colleagues studied subcutaneous IgG self-treatment for its immunomodulatory effects in ME/CFS patients with IgG or IgG subclass deficiency.

Araja and Latvian collaborators found that CFS/ME patients were not a risk group for COVID-19, though COVID-19 causes symptoms similar to CFS/ME and can result in a chronic post-viral CFS-like course.

Deumer et al. discuss the role of gut microbiota in CFS/ME disease progression and highlight non-coding RNA (ncRNA) as a potential diagnostic biomarker, suggesting SARS-CoV-2 infection may result in CFS-like symptoms.

Martin-Brufau and colleagues used EEG to show that fibromyalgia patients present lower levels of brain activity with reduced connectivity compared to controls, suggesting a possible neurophysiological pattern.

Rodriguez-Mansilla and Spanish collaborators found that an active exercise program improved pain, flexibility, static balance, perceived effort, and quality of life more effectively than wellness activities in fibromyalgia patients.
Lim and Son performed a meta-analysis comparing the prevalence of CFS/ME between Korea and Japan, addressing a lack of epidemiological data for these Asian countries.
Serum sVEGFR was significantly reduced in both PCS and PCS/CFS patients compared to healthy controls.
Despite reduced sVEGFR levels, free serum VEGF concentrations did not differ between patients and controls.
IL-18 serum levels were significantly decreased exclusively in PCS patients without ME/CFS compared to healthy controls.

A panel of vascular inflammation-associated serum cytokines/molecules (sCD40L, IL-6, IL-10, MCP-1, PIGF, sRAGE, sST2, TGF-β1, TNF-α, TNFSF14) showed largely no differences between PCS/PCS-CFS patients and healthy controls.
PCS/CFS patient serum showed significantly enhanced IgG autoantibody binding to both macrovascular (HUVEC) and microvascular (HDBEC) endothelial cells compared to healthy controls.
Unlike IgG, serum IgM autoantibody binding to HUVECs did not differ between patient groups and controls.
Total serum IgG concentrations were comparable across groups and did not correlate with AECA binding to HUVECs or HDBECs, ruling out a bias from bulk IgG levels.
Serum IgG binding to non-endothelial cell lines (HaCaT keratinocytes, A549 lung epithelial cells) did not significantly differ among groups, though reactivity trended higher in PCS/CFS.
PCS/CFS serum AECAs did not enhance complement-dependent cytotoxicity of HUVECs; instead, HUVEC lysis was reduced by PCS/CFS serum despite unchanged C3b deposition.
Both PCS and PCS/CFS serum significantly reduced surface expression of VCAM-1 and E-selectin on HUVECs compared to HC serum, rather than inducing an activated EC phenotype.
ICAM-1 surface expression on HUVECs was reduced exclusively following PCS/CFS serum treatment, distinguishing it from PCS.
Both PCS and PCS/CFS serum increased PECAM-1 surface levels on HUVECs compared to HC serum, contrary to the downregulation typically seen with EC activation.
sVCAM-1 release into HUVEC supernatant was increased following treatment with both PCS and PCS/CFS serum, mirroring the reduced surface VCAM-1 expression.
sICAM-1 release was increased exclusively following PCS/CFS serum treatment of HUVECs.
IGFBP-4 release from HUVECs was significantly enhanced by PCS/CFS serum compared to both HC and PCS serum, a molecule linked to anti-angiogenic effects and reduced NO-mediated vasodilation.
NGAL release from HUVECs was significantly increased following PCS serum treatment, part of a pro-angiogenic secretion profile specific to PCS.
MMP-9 release from HUVECs was significantly increased following PCS serum treatment, consistent with a pro-angiogenic ECM-degrading phenotype.
MPO release from HUVECs was increased by PCS serum, a molecule implicated in EC angiogenesis and nitric oxide consumption.
MRP8/14 release from HUVECs was increased following PCS serum treatment, a molecule implicated in neovascularisation.
Cystatin C release from HUVECs was reduced following PCS serum treatment, potentially facilitating protease-mediated ECM degradation and angiogenesis.
No significant group differences were found in HUVEC release of MMP-2, myoglobin, CRP, or SAA.
Unlike whole serum, treatment of HUVECs with plasma-derived extracellular vesicles from PCS or PCS/CFS patients did not alter the secretion profile compared to HC.
PCS serum significantly enhanced HUVEC tube formation (capillary-like junctions) in Matrigel assays compared to HC serum, whereas PCS/CFS serum did not promote angiogenesis.
When compared against the 90th percentile of the healthy control group, 8 of 11 PCS patient sera showed higher capillary junction numbers than most HC, versus only 4 of 8 PCS/CFS patient sera.
For total tube network mesh area, 5 of 11 PCS patients showed increased levels above the HC 90th percentile threshold, compared to none of the PCS/CFS patients.
Individuals with post-COVID-19, fibromyalgia, or chronic fatigue syndrome all reported elevated pain, fatigue, anxiety, depression, catastrophizing, and kinesiophobia.
Physical and cognitive function were similarly impacted across individuals with post-COVID-19, fibromyalgia, and chronic fatigue syndrome.
Individuals with post-COVID-19 reported lower pain and fatigue than those with fibromyalgia or chronic fatigue syndrome.
Comorbid diagnosis of post-COVID-19 with fibromyalgia and/or chronic fatigue syndrome further exacerbated pain, fatigue, and psychological symptom domains compared to post-COVID-19 alone.

A prior study cited in this protocol found that cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) produced positive effects on fatigue in adults with Q-fever fatigue syndrome immediately after treatment, but this effect was not maintained for most patients at 1-year follow-up.
The protocol cites an established relationship between the gut microbiome and fatigue, hypothesizing that a healthier diet could beneficially alter the microbiome and thereby reduce fatigue.
The protocol references prior evidence that nutritional/dietary advice can reduce some medically unresolved fatigue complaints in Dutch children.
A prior feasibility study found that the PROfeel experience-sampling-based personalized feedback method was considered feasible and useful by fatigued adolescents.
Passive transfer of IgG from complex regional pain syndrome patients into mice with skin incisions induced hypersensitivity to cold and heat stimulation compared to IgG from healthy individuals.

CSF levels of IL-1beta, IL-6 and TNF-alpha were significantly higher in CRPS patients compared to individuals with other pain syndromes and to healthy subjects.

Autonomic testing in CRPS patients showed warmer skin temperature in the acute stage and colder skin temperature in the chronic stage, with increased sweating in both stages, assessed at diagnosis and 2 years later.
Autoantibodies targeting autonomic nervous system receptors were detected in 40% of CRPS patients, suggesting an autoimmune basis for the disease.
Functional IgG autoantibodies directed against beta-2 adrenergic and muscarinic-2 receptors were detected in the serum of CRPS patients and showed pain-like properties.

P29ING4 autoantibodies showed higher specificity and sensitivity for CRPS compared to rheumatoid arthritis, axial spondyloarthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and healthy individuals, suggesting diagnostic utility.

Skin incisions in mice treated with IgG from longstanding CRPS patients showed prolonged swelling and hyperalgesia along with microglia and astrocyte activation in the dorsal horn and brain pain regions, compared to controls.

Passive transfer of serum from mice with induced fracture containing autoantibodies against autonomic nervous system receptors implicated these autoantibodies in trauma-related pain processing, supporting targeting the ANS for prevention/treatment of chronic post-traumatic pain such as CRPS.

Fibromyalgia patients were found to have a variety of autoantibodies including ANA and antithyroid antibodies, along with a high incidence of fibromyalgia among patients with autoimmune and rheumatic diseases.

Mice injected with IgG from fibromyalgia patients showed amplified responses to mechanical and cold stimulation compared to IgG from healthy people and IgG-depleted fibromyalgia patients, with the autoantibodies hyperstimulating nociceptive afferents in the dorsal root ganglia.

In 23 patients with chronic fatigue syndrome, tilt testing revealed significant alterations in sympathetic and parasympathetic function (expiratory-to-inspiratory ratio, systolic/diastolic blood pressure, heart rate) compared to healthy controls.
Autonomic dysfunction was strongly associated with fatigue severity in 40 patients with CFS compared to healthy age- and sex-matched controls.

In a cohort of 1226 CFS patients with cervical muscle-related complaints, autonomic nervous system involvement was documented, and recovery of patients after physical therapy was linked to amelioration of autonomic function.
Autoimmune etiology in CFS, including autoantibodies against neurotransmitters, has been reported as related to severe metabolic disturbances seen in patients with CFS.
High titers of antinuclear antibodies were found in 10 out of 11 symptomatic women with silicone breast implants, resembling autoantibodies found in idiopathic autoimmune diseases.

Among 116 women with silicone breast implants compared to 134 controls, a significantly increased incidence of autoantibodies against 15 of 20 autoantigens studied was detected, with about 20% having four autoantibodies and 8% having six autoantibodies.

Increased incidence of autoantibody production, particularly anti-SSB/La and anticollagen II, was reported in both symptomatic and asymptomatic women with silicone breast implants, with polyclonality more prominent in the symptomatic group and a correlation with implant duration.

Low serum levels of autoantibodies against autonomic nervous system GPCRs were detected in 93 women with silicone breast implants compared to 36 age-matched healthy women without implants, leading to the term 'autoimmune dysautonomia'.

Patients with COVID-19 showed significantly higher levels of autoantibodies than healthy subjects, and when injected into mice these autoantibodies disturbed immune function and exacerbated the disease course.

In 31 individuals with post-COVID complaints (mainly neurological), autoantibodies against GPCRs of the autonomic nervous system were detected in all patients, targeting beta2-adrenoreceptors, muscarinic receptors, and nociception-like opioid receptors, with both positive and negative chronotropic effects.

Objective cognitive task performance on the CogState battery was poorer, though mildly so, in participants meeting CFS criteria compared with both controls without disease and controls with a well-defined medical disorder (MS or rheumatoid arthritis).
Participants meeting CFS criteria reported substantially more subjective cognitive symptoms than controls without a medical disorder.
Participants meeting CFS criteria reported more subjective cognitive symptoms than participants with a well-defined medical disease (MS or rheumatoid arthritis).
Participants meeting fibromyalgia criteria reported substantially more subjective cognitive symptoms than controls without a medical disorder.
Participants meeting fibromyalgia criteria reported more subjective cognitive symptoms than participants with a well-defined medical disease (MS or rheumatoid arthritis).
